A 40-year-old intelligence officer has died in a road collision in Ukraine, the Ministry of Defence has confirmed.

Major Paul Wilks was killed in a traffic accident away from the front lines on Saturday 12 September.

Having commissioned from Sandhurst in 2012, he spent his entire military career serving in the Intelligence Corps.

His Commanding Officer described him as a "man of great intellect", who frequently spoke of his deep love for his wife and two sons.

Major Wilks completed multiple operational tours, including to Afghanistan, receiving two Operational Service Medals.

He was also awarded the Long Service and Good Conduct Medal on 7 May 2026.

His Commanding Officer said: “It is with profound sadness that we honour the memory of Major Paul Wilks.

“Even in high-pressure environments, Paul maintained a sharp sense of humour and a genuine warmth that connected him to everyone in this unit. He was a man of great intellect, yet he remained a mate to those he served with.

“He spoke often of his love for his wife and two sons, expressing his deep gratitude for the support they provided, which allowed him to serve with such distinction.

Major Paul Wilks spent his entire military career serving in the Intelligence Corps ( PA )

“It is because of that foundation that he was able to meet the challenges of his role, and it is in the course of his devotion to duty that he made the ultimate sacrifice.

“Major Wilks represented the finest traditions of UK Defence. It was a privilege to serve alongside him. We will miss him.”

Lieutenant General Matthew Jones, Colonel Commandant Intelligence Corps, described Major Wilks as “one of the most talented intelligence officers of his generation”.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: “Major Wilks served this country with pride and dedication. His loss will be deeply felt by those around him.

“The tributes paid by those who worked with Paul illustrate his exceptional talent and ability, underscored by genuine warmth, compassion and a desire to support others.

“His loss is a poignant reminder of the enormous sacrifice that our Armed Forces and their families make in the service of our country.

“My thoughts remain with his family, loved ones and colleagues.”

There is a small number of British personnel in Ukraine who provide security to diplomats and support the country’s armed forces.

British paratrooper George Hooley, 28, was killed in Ukraine in December when he watched Ukrainian forces testing a new defensive capability.

Severe gum bleeding and receding gums are linked to dementia risk rising by over 50 per cent in older adults, the results of a decade-long study of nearly 1,400 people in Japan suggest.

Dementia burden is increasing sharply worldwide, with the number of cases increasing from about 20 million in 1990 to 44 million in 2016, and is expected to increase to over 152 million by 2050, due to population ageing in many parts of the world.

A growing body of studies points to hidden oral health links to neurological diseases like dementia, but how they are connected remains a mystery.

There are many subtypes of dementia, of which Alzheimer's disease (AD) and vascular dementia (VaD) are the most common.

In the new study, researchers probed the link between dental health and the onset of dementia and its subtypes in a general population of older adults in Japan over 10 years.

They assessed the brain health of 1,396 participants aged over 60 years without dementia, and followed their status for 10 years.

Researchers found that over the years, 267 participants developed dementia, with Alzheimer’s disease diagnosed in 194 of them.

open image in gallery A dentist performs dental work for an American patient at the Rubio Dental Group offices in Los Algodones, Mexico ( AFP via Getty Images )

Gum bleeding was found in the majority of those diagnosed with Alzheimer’s, researchers say.

Those who experienced the most gum bleeding were 54 per cent likelier to develop dementia within the next ten years, scientists found.

They were also 61 per cent likelier to specifically develop Alzheimer's disease, according to the study.

Participants who had the worst receding gums had a 59 per cent higher risk of dementia, researchers found.

“These findings highlight the potential public health importance of preventing periodontitis to reduce the risk of dementia,” they wrote in The Journal of Clinical Periodontology.

Since the study is only observational, it doesn’t prove that poor gum health is causing dementia.

The findings point to a potential role of poor dental health in dementia development, scientists say.

“Periodontal care to improve and maintain periodontal health may help reduce the risk of dementia,” they wrote.

It is also likely that both gum disease and neurological conditions like dementia are triggered by a common root cause.

open image in gallery Attendees participate in "Lincoln Center Moments", a first-of-its-kind performance-based program created specifically for people living with dementia and their caregivers at Lincoln Center, in New York ( AFP via Getty Images )

Chronic inflammation across the whole body could be triggering both dementia and poor oral health, scientists suspect.

"Persistent systemic inflammation may impair the blood–brain barrier, allowing inflammatory mediators to penetrate the brain tissue and induce neuroinflammation and neuronal damage," the Japanese researchers say.

“One possible explanation is that infrequent toothbrushing promotes the accumulation of subgingival plaque and bacterial burden, which may contribute to systemic inflammation and increase dementia risk,” they say.

Citing a limitation of the study, researchers said it involved residents of a single municipality in Japan.

“Therefore, our findings have limited generalisability,” they said, adding that the results need to be confirmed in a larger study with more diverse participants.

“Further studies with a larger number of patients with vascular dementia are required to confirm these findings,” they wrote.

Sydney Sweeney is losing a massive amount of followers on Instagram after her controversial ad for a sports betting app.

The Euphoria actor, 29, has faced heaps of backlash since she appeared nude in a recent ad campaign for American gambling platform Novig, sparking criticism that the 60-second commercial — which features her strategically hiding parts of her naked body behind sports equipment — sexualizes female athletes and disrespects women as a whole.

Despite the backlash, Sweeney initially gained more followers on the platform in the days after she first shared the ad on Instagram last Wednesday.

Then, according to data gathered by social media analytics firm Social Blade, thousands of Sweeney’s followers hit the unfollow button Sunday — the same day that the actor appeared to respond to the criticism by wordlessly sharing pictures of female athletes who had previously taken pictures in the nude for magazine covers on her Instagram Story.

Sweeney lost 136,848 followers Sunday, according to the data, and another 66,446 on Monday. However, the 200,000 followers she lost make up less than one percent of her more than 25 million followers. Plus, in the days after the huge loss, she regained over 116,000 follows.

open image in gallery Sydney Sweeney's racy ad for sports betting site Novig has sparked controversy ( Getty )

The Independent has contacted Sweeney for further comment.

In what seemed to be her response to the backlash, Sweeney had posted nude campaigns of Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Caroline Wozniacki. She also highlighted male athletes who have done the same: Myles Garrett, Rob Gronkowski, Karl-Anthony Towns, and Jason Kelce.

She said in a statement about the ad last week: “The campaign was about embracing a fun idea. The concept is simple: cut through the noise and put the focus entirely on sports. The campaign brings that idea to life with confidence, humor and a playful edge.”

open image in gallery Sydney Sweeney has lost hundreds of thousands of Instagram followers since controversy over her nude ad ( Reuters )

Sweeney joined the sports prediction market platform as a strategic partner and equity holder.

Athletes from all over the world shared their distaste for the commercial after it was released.

Four-time Olympic swimming gold medalist Ariarne Titmus wrote on Instagram: “I can’t describe how infuriated I feel when I watch this. How do we live in a world where monetizing a woman’s body and sexualizing women’s sport is still a thing?”

After placing fourth in the 200 meters Sunday at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest, Hungary, British sprinter Amy Hunter said in a message to Sweeney on BBC: “Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like. Muscles, hard work, sweat, blood, tears.”

News.title: Man Utd’s week goes from bad to worse after embarrassing League Cup defeat fuels fan fury
News.content:
After a humiliating defeat to Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. All three goals will have Carrick and his analysts rewatching the footage in horror at how they conceded.

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” said Carrick. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

News.title: Spurs finally score... but still lose
News.content:
“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
Whatever his returns, there has been an extra focus to Brook’s approach this summer, possibly because he has learnt from a grievous indiscretion in Wellington last winter. While others chase the Indian Premier League, he is totally committed to England, taking his break while that tournament is on and playing every match in all formats for his country.

Brook had come to the crease at the fall of the first wicket and, while it is early days, England appear to have added another arrow to their quiver. They handed a debut to opener Aneurin Donald, with his cap presented in the pre-match huddle by Pietersen, the new “specialist mentor”.

Donald has been selected as an “intent merchant”, charged with going extremely hard from the first over, aping Phil Salt, who is missing with a quad injury. He did what he was asked to do, smearing his first ball for two, then pulling six to leg and hammering four through the offside before the first over was out. Another big shot, off Wellalage, in the second saw him well caught in the deep, but 12 off five had kickstarted the innings.

News.title: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town
News.content:
At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

The bond chaos came as Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, warned that Labour risked becoming “just a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos”.

He told LBC that John Healey’s original plan for a “low drama budget” had been “torpedoed” by higher borrowing costs and “events over the last couple of weeks”.

He said: “I think that [the bond market turmoil] will mean some hard choices next month at the Budget.”

“Few hard choices so far, but one is looming on the horizon, how any hole to the budget headroom is made good on. Is that a question of tax rises, or is it a question of taking the knife to public spending.”

Mr Haldane has been advising Labour since Andy Burnham took power.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

Sports.title: 'I'm an MK Dons legend after moving with them from Wimbledon – what happened was surreal'
Sports.content:
'I'm an MK Dons legend after moving with them from Wimbledon – what happened was surreal'

A former MK Dons star has reflected on his experience of the club relocating from Wimbledon

View 2 Images A former MK Dons star has discussed the club's move from Wimbledon (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Dean Lewington saw his career shaped by the hugely controversial decision to relocate and rename Wimbledon. The 42-year-old was part of the squad that experienced the club’s change of identity and remained with MK Dons until hanging up his boots last year.

‌



The defender rose through Wimbledon’s youth academy to make his debut in April 2003. Lewington featured for Wimbledon on 32 occasions and played his home matches at Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park, with the team having stopped using Plough Lane for first-team matches in 1991.

‌



When Lewington made his Wimbledon bow in the second tier, a proposed relocation to Milton Keynes had already been approved months earlier. In September 2003, shortly after facing the threat of liquidation, Wimbledon played their first game in Milton Keynes at the National Hockey Arena, officially becoming MK Dons the following season and later moving to Stadium MK in 2007.

‌



The seismic decision to relocate prompted a section of Wimbledon fans to form AFC Wimbledon, who are set to host MK Dons in a League One clash on Thursday. While some chose to support the fan-led team, Lewington remained and has reflected on finding a new home in Milton Keynes.

“It was really surreal. We trained in Milton Keynes a few times, but we were still training in London during the week, and then we came up for that game,” Lewington previously told BBC Three Counties Radio about his first experience of the National Hockey Arena. “I wasn’t in the squad so I was in the stands.

“It was just very surreal, it was all a bit strange. We were still Wimbledon, which was, I suppose, the bizarre part about it, really. You look back now and it seems kind of stupid that it wouldn’t have been Milton Keynes.

‌



“It was the blue and gold and it was all the team from Wimbledon, it was the youth team, like [Nigel] Reo-Coker was out there, and [Dean] Holdsworth and all those kinds of players. But you’re playing in Milton Keynes.”

View 2 Images Dean Lewington in action for Wimbledon at the National Hockey Stadium in 2003 (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Lewington remarkably made 917 appearances across 21 seasons with MK Dons and sits fourth in the all-time list for English league appearances on 820 games. The former defender, who has also had three stints as caretaker manager, won the EFL Trophy and reached the heights of the Championship with the club, eventually ending his career by playing in League Two.

There remains a clear rivalry between MK Dons and AFC Wimbledon, given the heartbreaking circumstances behind the formation of both clubs. However, Lewington has made it clear how he feels about the tension between the sides.

“I’m from the local area, [Wimbledon] was my local club,” Lewington said. “It still doesn’t entirely sit comfortably, what happened. You look back on it now and think, ‘Was it the right thing to do?’ And you just hope that everything was done with the right intentions. I know people probably debate that but I can sort of square it, if I think it was done with the right things in mind.”

Article continues below

He continued: “Now [MK Dons has] found its own feet and its own identity and AFC have found theirs. I think the best way to describe it is a father of two sons. You both have a claim to it but you’re both not it and that’s the only way I can really describe it.

“It was very surreal and I completely understand the anger behind it. I think the people that live in Milton Keynes would support us now. If you said we were going to uproot this club and take it to Boston, I think they’d understand the anger behind it.”

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Martin Zubimendi set for new role as furious player forces Mikel Arteta's hand
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Martin Zubimendi set for new role as furious player forces Mikel Arteta's hand

Arsenal's Carabao Cup victory over Ipswich Town has given Mikel Arteta plenty to think about

View Image Martin Zubimendi took on a new role for Mikel Arteta this week (Image: 2025 The Arsenal Football Club Plc)

Arsenal continued their fine form on Tuesday evening with a convincing win over Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup third round. Mikel Arteta will take his team to Brighton on Saturday as the Premier League resumes, looking to keep their place at the top of the table.

‌



The Gunners beat Ipswich 4-2 at Portman Road, easing into the fourth round. While the victory maintained their perfect start to the season, it also provided its fair share of talking points.

‌



One of which revolves around the future of the currently out-of-favour Martin Zubimendi. He impressed the Arsenal faithful in an unfamiliar role against the Tractor Boys.

‌



Gunners' youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly also made headlines with his behaviour at full-time, forcing an intervention from Arteta. Here, we take a closer look at both stories.

Zubimendi set for new role

Spanish midfielder Zubimendi has found minutes hard to come by this season, but was shifted to right-back for Tuesday night's fixture, where he excelled.

Premier League panel unanimously agree on Arsenal red card controversy in final verdict READ MORE :

Man Utd could lose millions on JJ Gabriel as favourites to sign youngster emerge READ MORE :

The 27-year-old has experience of the role, featuring in the same spot on the final day of last season when Arsenal won 2-1 away to Crystal Palace.

‌



The position may now offer him his best chance of getting back into the Gunners' first XI after Ben White suffered a groin niggle in the 2-0 win at Sunderland last Saturday. White has been a regular starter this season as Jurrien Timber steps up his recovery from a minor groin procedure earlier this summer.

Zubimendi was involved in Max Dowman's second goal against Ipswich and was also impressive from a defensive point of view, cementing his claims to take on the role from White and Timber.

Zubimendi, who signed for Arsenal in the summer of 2025 from Real Sociedad, could now be set to solve Arsenal's right-back conundrum for the time being after his confident performance on Tuesday night.

‌

Lewis-Skelly

Gunners' boss Arteta had to escort an angry Lewis-Skelly away from the officials after Arsenal's victory over Ipswich. The Tractor Boys' two consolation goals came with Arsenal 4-0 to the good.

Anis Mehmeti and former Arsenal striker Chuba Akpom spared Ipswich from a mauling, but the latter's goal was a point of contention. Akpom seemingly dragged Lewis-Skelly to the floor in the build-up to his strike, with referee Peter Bankes waving away appeals.

‌



With VAR not in use in the Carabao Cup until the last four, the goal was given. Lewis-Skelly fumed at that decision and remonstrated with the officials at full-time, trailing them as they walked to the centre circle.

Mikel Merino attempted to calm Lewis-Skelly before Arteta marched over, asserting his authority, as he twice told the youngster to walk away. Shortly after, Akpom appeared to joke about the incident with Arsenal stars Bukayo Saka and Konsa.

Saka appeared to quiz Akpom if it had been a foul, with the Ipswich forward nodding. Akpom joined the Gunners at the age of six and made his debut for the North Londoners under Arsene Wenger in 2013.

Sports.title: Man Utd crash out of the Carabao Cup after crumbling vs Brighton - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Manchester United's season went from bad to worse as they gave up a 2-0 lead to lose to Brighton and go crashing out of the Carabao Cup.

Goals inside the opening ten minutes from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount looked to have set the home side on their way to a much needed win, given the difficult start to their campaign.

But Pascal Gross, who scored his eighth goal against the Red Devils, helped the Seagulls record yet another win over the side from Manchester. United hadn't given up a two-goal lead to lose at Old Trafford since the 1970s, but that stat went up in smoke.

Charalampos Kostoulas pulled a goal back in first-half stoppage time before Gross equalised midway through the second-half. Maxim De Cuyper completed the comeback on the 70 minute mark to send shivers around Old Trafford.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lacey's strike after eight minutes came after he cut in from the right, taking his left-footed shot early, which flew into the near post. The Old Trafford crowd still reeling from that strike were celebrating again within two minutes.

Mount, who himself has found opportunities hard to come by, was able to seize on an error of Brighton's own making as they attempted to play out from the back. The United midfielder struck his volley into the ground, with the bounce seeing it nestle into the Brighton net.

‌



The Seagulls rallied and eventually got their reward in first-half stoppage time. Kostoulas was able to finish from an acute angle to half the deficit. Little did he know it would ignite a historic comeback. Gross' equaliser owed to some poor defending as a headed clearance from the halfway line found the Brighton man unmarked on the edge of the United box before he turned and finished.

View 4 Images Pascal Gross continued his impressive scoring record against Man Utd

De Cuyper's winner came from close range as he converted after a neat comeback before running towards the corner where the travelling supporters were enjoying another day out in Manchester.

Marcus Rashford missed United's best chance to level as he was denied from close range as the Red Devils saw their Carabao Cup hopes ended at the first hurdle once again. Here's five talking points from Old Trafford.

‌



Brighton jinx continues

In recent years few teams have enjoyed greater dominance over United than the Seagulls, who have made beating them an annual event. Brighton headed to Old Trafford having won seven of their last eleven games against the Premier League giants.

That includes a 2-1 win in Manchester in the third round of the FA Cup last season. That run of form also saw Brighton beat United in the first game of the Erik ten Hag era, that another win at Old Trafford, and a 4-0 mauling back in 2022 when the Red Devils were at one of their lowest ebbs.

You may have thought that a two-goal head start would've been enough to see United get the better of Brighton, but no, the Seagulls recorded another impressive win - their eighth in their last 12 against the Red Devils.

Game mismanagement

Throughout the season United have faced criticism for failing to manage games and, worryingly for them, conceding goals. Sunday was one of the rare occasions they didn't concede twice during a game, but that trend returned on Wednesday as Brighton breached the United goal on numerous occasions.

‌



View 4 Images Michael Carrick had no answers as his side lost for the third time this season

Perhaps a greater frustration for Carrick will the apparent inability of his side to manage games, especially when leading. They failed to see out the contest at Everton recently, conceding late. Against the ten-men of Manchester City they also failed to make it count. But the loss to Brighton by far and away topped the lot.

Lacey's moment

The last time Lacey faced Brighton at Old Trafford he was thrown on after an hour, but failed to see the full-time whistle after being shown a red card. The teenager cut a despondent figure when he walked down the tunnel, thinking one of his early opportunities to impress had come and gone.

Eight months after that forgettable moment the teenager, handed his first start of the season, needed just eight minutes to score the first goal of the night. There are high hopes for Lacey, even in an attack that has established quality, and the 19-year-old's first goal of his career could not have come against a better opponent, even if his efforts will be forget on what was a difficult night for those in red.

‌



View 4 Images Shea Lacey's strike was the perfect start for the hosts

No place for JJ

All the talk regarding United over the past 24 hours is shock as they deal with the bombshell news that JJ Gabriel, one of the most highly thought of players to come through the academy for some time, wants out.

The sensation was named Under-18 Premier League player of the year last season, even though he was only 14 when the campaign began, underlining his potential. He was poised to make his debut against Brighton, but instead is looking for a way out of Old Trafford. His name alongside the No 77 was printed on the back of the matchday programme, but his stay in Manchester could be over before its started.

Sesko pressure remains

In the opening weeks of the season there's been constant theories as to why Carrick doesn't seem to fancy Sesko, at least as a starter. The Slovenian grew into his debut season, coming off the bench to score multiple winners, but a bench player he has remained.

‌



Instead players who aren't natural No 9s have been deployed in those positions ahead of Sesko. But when the former RB Leipzig man got the nod on Wednesday night he did little to push his case for more involvement, especially from the start. Being hooked on the hour mark was not a ringing endorsement.

Sports.title: Liverpool send clear message to Arsenal over 'genuine' plan to poach Rio Ngumoha
Sports.content:
Liverpool send clear message to Arsenal over 'genuine' plan to poach Rio Ngumoha

Rio Ngumoha has transfer interest from Arsenal but Liverpool have a clear stance on selling the young attacker

View 2 Images Liverpool star Rio Ngumoha is not for sale amid transfer interest from Arsenal (Image: (Photo by James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Liverpool have reportedly issued a hands-off warning to Arsenal and other clubs interested in signing Rio Ngumoha. Bayern Munich were linked with a move during the summer transfer window, and now the Gunners have emerged as a club that wants to sign the exciting winger.

‌



Ngumoha joined Liverpool from Chelsea in 2024 and signed a three-year professional contract 12 months ago. He has made 35 appearances for Liverpool's senior team, with Andoni Iraola continuing to give him more minutes this season.

‌



The 18-year-old started Tuesday's Carabao Cup third round win over Tottenham, but Arsenal are keeping a close eye on whether his minutes decrease following the arrivals of Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz, according to The Daily Mail.

‌



Liverpool news: Reds confirm midfielder return as star admits regret at Anfield exit READ MORE :

Arsenal handed final verdict as Premier League panel unanimously agree on red card decision READ MORE :

However, it has been claimed that Liverpool have no plans to entertain any offers and remain keen on agreeing a new contract with the teenager. Interest from Arsenal is understood to be genuine, but a deal is not advanced.

He has two years left on his current deal and Liverpool want to keep him beyond that as there is a belief he can become a 'world-beater'.

Ngumoha is believed to know of the interest from elsewhere, but he is enjoying life and is therefore happy at Liverpool. There is also no current update on contract talks between the two parties.

‌



Arsenal's hope that Ngumoha will become restless appears far-fetched as the winger has already been deployed from the off in four games this season, which means he is nearly halfway to the nine starts he managed last season.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

One of those was the Champions League clash against Atletico Madrid, with Ngumoha speaking fondly of the experience and the trust placed in him by Iraola.

‌



“It was crazy,” Ngumoha told the club’s website. “In the morning when I knew when the gaffer put out the team, I saw my name there. I was like, 'Yeah, today's going to be a good day!'

“A first start in the Champions League, especially at Anfield and against a good side. To get the three points and just hear the fans, like I said the other day, Anfield was roaring, I couldn't ask for much more.

View 2 Images Ngumoha was buzzing to start Liverpool's first Champions League game of the season

‌



“Like I said, the gaffer, [for him] to put faith in me and to show me that he believes in my abilities and qualities to help the team get a win is really positive. I couldn't ask for much more.”

Ngumoha started on his favoured left side in that game, but has been needed on the other flank a few times already, with all of Barcola, Munoz and Cody Gakpo preferring to play on that side.

The latter can play as the striker, while Munoz has performed admirably when on the right with his tireless work ethic, earning praise. He also scored his first Liverpool goal when on that side, with a superb strike against Nottingham Forest.

Article continues below

The four have shared minutes so far with Ngumoha set for a considerable amount of game time, given the competitions Liverpool are in this season.

Sports.title: Biggest VAR blunders ranked after Man City's derby winner leads to Enzo Maresca swipe
Sports.content:
The VAR fallout rumbles on, as it always does. The Manchester derby is the latest game to be embroiled in controversy that stems from decisions taken at Stockley Park.

Erling Haaland's strike was enough to land Manchester City the three points on Sunday, leaving those associated with Manchester United fuming. Michael Carrick didn't shy away from lamenting the decision in the aftermath of the game.

Pro Ref chief Howard Webb has quickly come out and owned up to the error live on TV, after the organisation itself had issued an apology to United within hours of the final whistle.

Once again the issue of VAR and those using it is front and centre. Since 2019 we've had the system in use, and yet the sceptics seem no closer to being converted. Even some of those in favour initially have veered towards binning it, letting mangers and players live with decisions as we did for decades.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

City boss Enzo Maresca has claimed the reaction to the VAR blunder, which failed to acknowledge that Enzo Fernandez had thrown himself at the ball from an offside position, had been overblown.

"Talking about one episode or one moment after that game when we played for 70- 75 minutes with 10 players, I think it's quite poor," said the Italian.

‌



He too claimed that some decisions go for you, some go against you. Maresca even went as far as to reference another VAR mishap in a Manchester derby in 2023, when he was an assistant to Pep Guardiola. The refereeing body didn't apologise for that one.

View 6 Images VAR awarded the goal after it was initially ruled out for offside (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Any mistake that lives with someone for three years is clearly noteworthy, but we haven't lacked for errors of that magnitude. So what really is VAR's darkest day? We've had a go at ranking the biggest injustices, but make sure you have a go at putting them in order yourself using our interactive tool.

5. Haaland's derby winner

The latest one that's got us all talking. Haaland's strike on Sunday was initally ruled offside, and it looked it, but once the lines had been drawn it was deemed that Patrick Dorgu had played him onside.

‌



That part is accepted, what isn't accepted is that Fernandez had no bearing on the play. The Argentine midfielder was stood in the middle of the box in an offside position and threw himself to try and head the ball, but missed. Lisandro Martinez was clearly impeded as he attempted to cover Fernandez and Haaland.

VAR claimed that because Fernandez didn't touch the ball, all was cleared. Failing to acknowledge the fact he clearly impacted the play. Gary Neville said that he expected an apology pretty soon, and one duly arrived.

4. Rodri dodges handball

During the 2021/22 title race City went to Goodison Park and scored late on via Phil Foden as they looked to pick up a priceless three points. That was soon in doubt though, when Rodri looked to have handled the ball in his own box.

The Spaniard misjudged the bounce of the ball and, as he went to control it on his chest, looked to have seen the ball strike his arm instead. The home crowd were adamant and, such was the length of the VAR check, it was clearly a tight call.

‌



View 6 Images Rodri escaped any punishment as VAR overlooked this handball shout (Image: Sky Sports)

To the naked eye it looked as if the City talisman had made a rare error, but somehow he and Pep Guardiola escaped. Lampard accused the VAR official Chris Kavanagh of being a “professional who cannot do his job right”. Then referees’ chief Mike Riley would personally apologised to Lampard, for whatever that was worth.

3. Fernandes goal given

The one Maresca just refuses to forget. In 2023 City took the lead at Old Trafford before two goals from United turned the game. Bruno Fernandes' strike levelled the game and came despite Marcus Rashford being offside by several yards.

The United attacker raced after the ball and had in it his path, albeit he didn't touch it, but his presence undoubtedly influenced the City defenders. Fernandes then raced from an onside position to score. The offside flag went up, but the officials then reversed their decision as the hosts went on to land a winner.

‌



View 6 Images Marcus Rashford was clearly offside and chased after the ball, but didn't touch it, with Man Utd profiting as a result (Image: Sky Sports)

"Rashford is offside. Bruno Fernandes is not offside. The question is intervening or not intervening in the action," said Guardiola. "When one player shoots and [another] player is in front of the keeper and does not touch the ball, it's disallowed all the time."

Webb later claimed: “I think if that exact circumstance happens again you would probably see a different outcome".

2. Onana punch overlooked

In Erik ten Hag's second year at the helm he decided to rid of David de Gea and bring in Andre Onana, a move that would not prove overly successful. On his first outing the warning signs were evident with the Cameroonian.

‌



As United looked to close out three points in their opening fixture against Wolves, who had been more than good value for a point if not more, Onana had a moment of madness and came out to punch clear a cross, but instead caught Sasa Kalajdzic. No contact made with the ball, but contact certainly made with the Wolves player in the dying stages.

View 6 Images Andre Onana collided with Wolves star Sasa Kalajdzic, but dodged any punishment

No penalty though. Then Wolves boss Gary O'Neil said elite referees manager Jon Moss told him he "could not believe" the error. The three officials involved were overlooked the following weekend.

1. Diaz goal ruled out

Liverpool's first defeat of 2023 came at Tottenham on an evening when Luis Diaz thought he'd scored the opening goal of the night, only to quickly see the offside flag raised.

‌



It looked a tight call to the naked eye and so VAR jumped in to confirm the linesman's call. The glaring issue? They thought the call was onside, so when they 'agreed' with the on-field call, they were agreeing it was offside.

The PGMOL called it a "significant human error" and the audio, later released, showed immediate panic and several people not on the same page. Explicits rang out once they realised the gravity of the error and, after the game restarted they couldn't call it back and simply had to live with their mistake.

View 6 Images Luis Diaz's wrongly disallowed goal at Tottenham three years ago remains one of VAR's darkest days (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Then Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp was quizzed on the apology from the PGMOL but replied: "We won't get points for it. We all thought that when VAR came in it would make things easier."

‌



Now it's your turn...rank these in order, with the most egregious error taking top spot...

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel snubbed for Man Utd vs Brighton as three decisions 'rile his dad'
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel snubbed for Man Utd vs Brighton as three decisions 'rile his dad'

Michael Carrick's Manchester United squad to face Brighton and Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup does not include JJ Gabriel following the teenagers stunning request

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel told Manchester United he wants to leave (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

JJ Gabriel has not been included in Manchester United's squad to face Brighton in the Carabao Cup following the explosive news that he had asked to quit the club. The 15-year-old had been expected to be included at Old Trafford as he awaits his senior debut after featuring during pre-season.

‌



But the decision has been taken not to include him among Michael Carrick's options on Wednesday evening. Despite the starlet sending formal notice of his desire to become a free agent, United believe the situation can be resolved.

‌



Gabriel is not able to sign a professional contract until he turns 17, and scholarship agreements are not permitted until players turn 16. He remains registered to the club as Premier League rules require all parties to come to an agreement to end a registration period early.

‌



“During your child’s registration period, their registration may only be cancelled if everyone agrees (the club, player and their parent/carer)," they state.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“If the parties don’t agree, then any person involved can also ask the Premier League to provide a binding decision on a termination request," the rules add.

‌



Last week, Gabriel wiped all of the images from his Instagram, leading to some concern. It has since emerged that Gabriel's father, Joe O'Cearuill, has taken issue with how United have handled his son's development, with three areas in particular proving problematic.

The Daily Mail reports that O'Cearuill wanted to see his son accelerated even faster to the first team picture, despite playing for the under-21 side at 15. There was also frustration that Gabriel was not included in squads to face Ipswich and Sabah, where some believed there was a suitable option for the youngster to make his first-team bow.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has requested to leave Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Gabriel instead scored a hat-trick against Sabah's youth side as United thrashed their opponents 5-0 in the UEFA Youth League. The Red Devils had 44 shots to Sabah's zero.

Youngster Shea Lacey, 19, has been provided with the opportunity to star against the Seagulls. The winger did appear against Sabah in the Champions League for an 18-minute cameo and also featured for 10 minutes in defeat to Hull City after an impressive pre-season.

‌



Carrick's full-back options have been diminished for the clash with neither Luke Shaw or Patrick Dorgu in the squad. Either Noussair Mazraoui or Diogo Dalot will start on the left with Harry Amass an option from the bench, after spending last season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich.

Benhamin Sesko also comes into the lineup having been confined to substitute appearances in the Premier League. Big-hitters in the form of Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire all start from the bench.

Sports.title: 'Nothing wrong with his recovery' – Red Bull provide Hadjar update
Sports.content:
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies says they will continue to prioritise Isack Hadjar's recovery over rushing his return from injury, with evaluations planned before a call on whether he races at next week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Hadjar has missed the last three races after sustaining a wrist injury during routine training ahead of the sport's return to action from its summer break. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson has stood in for him.

Speaking after last Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix, Mekies said Hadjar's recovery was going to plan, with a simulator session planned to help assess his readiness for any return to action in Baku.

"There is nothing wrong with Isack's recovery. I think we have learned that it's fundamentally a normal time for the sort of injuries he has," said Mekies

"So, we will continue with the same approach and what we have.

"We will evaluate the situation in a week's time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Craig Slater explained Isack Hadjar's wrist injury ahead of the Dutch GP, the first race the Frenchman missed

"We have a full week, a bit more than a full week, to evaluate situations, to see how he feels and then to put him on the simulator, to expose him to real-life constraints.

"And if he feels close to 100 per cent, we go for it. If he feels the recovery is not completed, we will stick to our approach to put his recovery first.

"What we don't want to do is, by having an early return, compromise his long-term capacity to come back to 100 per cent."

The Azerbaijan GP, held on a street circuit in Baku, is the first round of a triple header with races in Malaysia and Singapore following on the subsequent two weekends.

Red Bull pleased with Lawson's 'very good' stand-in performances

Lawson has stepped up from sister Racing Bulls to cover for Hadjar, with the New Zealander returning to a seat he briefly held in an ill-fated two-race stint at the start of last season. Yuki Tsunoda has been driving for Racing Bulls.

Lawson has twice qualified eighth and scored points at both Zandvoort and Madrid, where he was sixth.

"I think he's done a very good job," said Mekies.

"I think we all know how difficult it is to jump to a different team, to a different car, and I think he has done that to the best of what could have been our expectations.

"He has taken some very important points [in Madrid] with the P6. He did the same in Zandvoort, and in Monza he would have done something similar without the contact with Nico [Hulkenberg] and the damage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix

"So, I think he did a very good job. Again, very different pictures compared to the first races of 2025 when he was in the team, so we are thankful and happy with that."

Lawson has rebuilt his form and confidence at Racing Bulls over the past year and was already enjoying a consistent points-scoring season before his unexpected temporary senior Red Bull return.

"I think he has continued to grow as a driver," added Mekies, who has worked with Lawson at both Red Bull teams. "He's very calm in the car; he's very focused.

"He's certainly making... I don't know if he makes an effort or not [to do it], but he's certainly managed to keep things simple in the way he tracks with the team and in the way he tackles his own performance and the car performance.

"So, he's focused on the essentials; he tries to get the basics right, and it's working for him. Of course, with more time in the car, you can then get to another degree of finesse, maybe.

"But I think that, of course, is very, very strong."

Sports.title: New season, same Man Utd story - Carrick is now firmly feeling the pressure
Sports.content:
This wasn't just a defeat. This wasn't just a collapse. This wasn't just a cup exit. Another Manchester United managerial project is heading in that one, same direction. And even Michael Carrick recognises that.

"We've gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that," he said. "I'm happy enough to be honest about that. That's how it feels."

It's a story that's been seen before. A dismal Carabao Cup experience at the first hurdle - this time throwing away a 2-0 lead to exit to Brighton - harks back to memories of Ruben Amorim's disappointing defeat at Grimsby last year, which helped signal the beginning of the end.

A cup exit to the Seagulls was also reminiscent of the FA Cup defeat United suffered to Fabian Hurzeler's side at the start of the year. That was the last match before Carrick returned to the club and sparked a mini-revival. Now it seems like United are back to square one again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the third round of the Carabao Cup match between Manchester United and Brighton

Even Pascal Gross scoring the equaliser at Old Trafford brought back memories of how he netted twice at United's home in August 2022 to put Erik ten Hag's tenure on the back foot, in the same way Carrick is facing an uphill battle now.

Gross still doing the business four years later is a great testament to the German's longevity at 35 years old - but it's an even more damning reflection of United's lack of progression in that time.

Since that match in 2022, which came 1,502 days ago, Gross has secured European football for Brighton, left the club for Borussia Dortmund, rejoined the Seagulls, got them back into Europe, watched on as United spent £365m on seven new central midfielders - and still he stood tall above the United midfield.

Image: Brighton's Pascal Gross, right, celebrates after scoring his side's second goal

Around £140m of that pot started for United against Brighton in Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount and Andrey Santos, while a further £70m in Carlos Baleba watched on from the stands as his old club beat his new one. What must he be thinking?

Just like against Hull on the opening weekend of the season, United were outfought by Brighton. "They didn't look fit enough," said Jamie Redknapp. "I don't know if a lot of them do enough. I saw too many players not running back or not looking fit enough."

Many can point towards the nine changes Carrick made, with many of United's players coming into the team after weeks on the Premier League bench. But Brighton also made six changes to their regular line-up, including first starts for the club to four summer signings. What was their excuse?

Once again, the lack of investment in the defensive positions during the transfer market was very clear. The warnings about not addressing that position were there - and a big reason for Brighton turning the game on its head was the defensive displays of Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven.

Image: Michael Carrick looks on glumly as his Manchester United side were beaten by Brighton

"The inexperience of the two young centre-backs definitely showed," said Redknapp. "The pair of them were just inept in everything they did. If you look at Luka Vuskovic, who is 18 or 19, at this level he has aggression, winning challenges, recovery runs.

"And you looked at the two who played at United who played like everything was easy, making bad decisions - there was a difference in Brighton's defending when it came to going about their business."

The difference was seen in the second goal, as Vuskovic won a header ahead of Benjamin Sesko and the ball ran straight through the heart of the United defence for Gross to score easily.

Heaven was caught on his heels and failed to come across. "He doesn't anticipate the danger. Sprint, get to the penalty spot. But he's jogging.

"And Yoro, what kind of an effort is that to stop the shot? How easy was that? This isn't a five-a-side competition."

And for the third goal, Yoro was caught jogging back again as Brighton broke to score - not only highlighting Redknapp's defensive concerns about United, but their fitness ones too. "You've got to sprint Leny," he said. "He's jogging. If he sprints, he gets back and makes that block."

But while United are making familiar mistakes, they are still making unwanted history.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick responds to the Old Trafford boos after Manchester United were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton

Not only was this the first time in 50 years that an opposition team has won at Old Trafford having been 2-0 down in the game, but it was the first time United have lost at home after holding a half-time lead in 551 half-time leads.

The time before the defeat to Brighton came in 1984, which pre-dated Sir Alex Ferguson's time at the club. Throw in a joint-worst start to a Premier League season after four games and the pressure is really growing on Carrick.

United's only win so far this season has been a 5-2 win over Ipswich that saw United struggle for the best part of an hour. And while there have been some mitigating factors - worldies at Everton and a contentious Manchester derby winner - there have been too many of those to be one-offs already.

Fulham

Manchester United Sunday 20th September 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

It all sets up a massive Super Sunday game this weekend away at winless Fulham, facing their own early woes under Alvaro Arbeloa. What follows is a three-week international break which is prime time for an early managerial change.

A win at Craven Cottage buys Carrick time. Defeat and it will be a long period of questions.

Sports.title: Broadhurst: 'This is my last shot at the Olympics'
Sports.content:
The European Elite Boxing Championships begin in Sofia, Bulgaria on Thursday with GB entering a strong team dotted with Commonwealth Games gold medallists.

Amy Broadhurst, a former World and European gold medallist for Ireland, will be part of the squad boxing for Britain.

Broadhurst, a key sparring partner for Katie Taylor for the Irish legend's first iconic victory over Amanda Serrano, switched from Ireland to Britain ahead of Paris 2024 as she sought to qualify for the Olympic Games.

These European championships will be her first major championships since returning to competition after the birth of her baby boy.

"It's tough but we're making it work and I'm very lucky to have the support around me," Broadhurst told Sky Sports. "He's at the right age now where this is possible.

"He'll come to Bulgaria with me and he comes to Sheffield every second week with me," she continued. "Those weeks are tough because you're doing two jobs then.

"This is my last shot at the Olympics. So they know after this it's all said and done."

Image: Amy Broadhurst is a World Championships gold medallist taking one last chance to reach the Olympic Games.

These Europeans will be a key step on a journey that she hopes will eventually take her to LA 2028. But her return to boxing has already been eventful. The first bout in her comeback earlier this year saw her drawn against her old team.

"My first fight back after two years was against Ireland. So that was a mad situation," she said.

"I was trying to control my feelings because obviously a lot of [stuff] went on with that whole situation.

"I knew going in that I was going to do okay. But there was just a lot of ill feelings on both behalfs. I think I handled it very well. I shook hands with the coach and I showed respect. That was probably the main thing, not to get sucked into the emotional part of it. It was get in, box and move on. It was like closing the chapter on something. We shook hands and then that's it."

Image: Amy Broadhurst with her 2022 Commonwealth Games gold medal.

She didn't box Ireland's top lightweight then but that could potentially happen in Sofia. Kellie Harrington, Ireland's two-time Olympic champion, has entered these Europeans.

"I was her sparring partner for the 2021 Games," Broadhurst said. "I was brought over to Tokyo.

"We've shared the ring many times and it would be a spicy fight.

"You could meet each other," Broadhurst noted. "You just don't know what's going to happen.

"I'll take it one fight at a time."

Sports.title: De Cuyper and Brighton pile on pain for Manchester United with comeback
Sports.content:
Across four days Manchester United have lost the 199th derby against Manchester City, were told by JJ Gabriel that he wants to leave, and now they have been knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton.

Capitulating after being 2-0 up may be the pick of these dizzying blows, as the prolonged boos at the final whistle suggested, and doing so ends a proud 50-year record: the last time the same lead at Old Trafford ended in defeat was Tottenham’s 3-2 win in September 1976.

When Marcus Rashford skated in with the chance to take the tie to 3-3 late on, there was no surprise he hit Jason Steele rather than the net.

Towards the end, Matheus Cunha was thrown on to join Bruno Fernandes, also a late substitute, illustrating how desperate Michael Carrick was. Yet Charalampos Kostoulas went close to scoring a second for Brighton, as United could not find a route to cancelling out Maxim De Cuyper’s 69th-minute strike that proved the winner.

After taking only four points from 12 in the league, serious questions will now be asked about where Carrick’s team are heading; they have to beat Fulham on Sunday to start correcting a dismal start to the season. The manager already looks haunted and he talked afterwards of not caring about being under pressure.

View image in fullscreen United’s evening started brightly enough, with the 19-year-old Shea Lacey scoring on his first start for the club. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Carrick said the injustice suffered against City on Sunday would give his side an edge and Shea Lacey provided one when decorating a full debut with the sweetest of goals. The 19-year-old shimmied in Brighton’s area, beating Jaouen Hadjam before firing beyond a helpless Jason Steele. As impressive here was Benjamin Sesko’s hold-up work in the buildup as this allowed red shirts to flood forward, Youri Tielemans feeding Lacey.

This was eight minutes in and less than 120 seconds later Mason Mount doubled United’s advantage. Rashford’s pace and drive took him clear along the left, again inside the area. A trailing Steele boot saved the No 9’s effort but the ball bounced into Mount’s path and he drove home, via the turf, for a first goal since a win at Wolves last December.

Lacey’s strike drew a Carrick grin and delight from Mount, and you wondered how Gabriel – earmarked for the squad in this game, with the chance to become United’s youngest player – felt.

Brighton had lost only one of their previous five visits here and a flying start to the league campaign has Fabian Hürzeler’s team in fifth. Yet the 5-0 hammering of Coventry on Sunday already seemed distant as United continued to dominate.

View image in fullscreen Charalampos Kostoulas started Brighton’s comeback just before half-time. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

Olivier Boscagli hit a corner straight out, summing up the visitors’ start, before Matt O’Riley forced Ayden Heaven into an error that led to another. This presaged a Seagulls renaissance that featured a lightning Malick Yalcouyé break but, clear in on the debutant Karl Darlow’s goal, the Ivorian spooned wide. The No 35 lacked the sharpness evident in a Rashford nutmeg of Chema Andrés which embarrassed the Brighton man and when Pascal Gross blasted over this was one more chance spurned by Hürzeler’s men.

But then came a goal – and real hope – for Brighton. Hadjam’s long left-right diagonal cut United’s rearguard clean out, and the slumbering Heaven allowed Kostoulas to scamper free, the striker beating Darlow through his legs.

Carrick, having beaten only Ipswich in the league and Sabah in Europe so far this season, needed a win, and as United (not under him) exited at the earliest opportunity in both domestic cups last season, progressing to at least a second tie in one of them would be welcome.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A wild Tielemans long-range shot that ballooned over failed to restore United’s two-goal lead but at least the home team were tapping the ball about, operating in Brighton territory, moving the visitors around.

View image in fullscreen United were frustrated by Pascal Gross’s leveller for Brighton, but things were about to get even worse for Michael Carrick’s side. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

A Sesko burst from halfway had the onrushing Steele hacking away just in time. United were in control. But the question was: could they maintain this and register the type of mature, accomplished display that would show an evolution in Carrick’s team? Sesko, in yards of space, dawdling and being dispossessed when a simple ball would have fed Lacey, suggested not.

A loose Rashford pass aimed for Sesko hinted at the same. More promising was a pass for Noussair Mazraoui as he drove into the area along the left channel, as was the subsequent corner that created an opening Tielemans narrowly missed.

Quick Guide Carabao Cup roundup: Fleetwood handed win over Blades Show A 57th-minute Rhys Norrington-Davies own goal sent Fleetwood into the last 16 of the Carabao Cup for the first time as the League Two club stunned their Championship opponents, Sheffield United, 1-0 at Highbury, before pulling a home tie against Arsenal out in the draw. Matt Lawlor’s side, unbeaten now in nine games in all competitions, had another Danny Andrew effort ruled out for offside and twice hit the woodwork in a dominant second-half display. It was a searching left-wing cross from Andrew that Norrington-Davies nodded beyond Michael Cooper to give the fourth-tier club a historic victory. Tom Cannon did get the ball in the net for Chris Wilder’s visitors who lined up with only four starting survivors from last Friday’s 1-0 league defeat by Wolves. But a flag for offside was raised before the striker slid the ball into the net. United started positively and Ollie Arblaster had a goalbound effort blocked after only 36 seconds. But Mark Helm forced Cooper into a seventh-minute save before the former United forward Ched Evans put his follow-up header narrowly wide. Jay Lynch denied Joe Rothwell as the visitors attacked again but Cooper was the busier, saving from Lewis McCann and Crispin McLean. Helm’s dipping right-foot effort from 18 yards grazed the top netting as Fleetwood finished the first half in the ascendancy and they deserved their break from Norrington-Davies’ own goal. United finally came to life in the last 10 minutes with Lynch brilliantly denied Sydie Peck and Ben Brereton Díaz, while Cannon saw a goalbound strike superbly blocked. Everton’s forgotten man Charly Alcaraz stepped up when his side needed some inspiration to score the only goal in the win over Wolves three minutes after coming on. The Argentinian had played just 14 minutes all season but belied his lack of match sharpness with a quick switch of the ball from one foot to the other to guide a left-footed shot past the former Everton goalkeeper João Virgínia in the 80th minute. It also represented a minor success for Tyler Dibling, whose career has not really taken off since his £35m move from Southampton just over a year ago, as he claimed the assist at the end his most encouraging performance for the club. Everton's reward is a home tie against Newcastle. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But then calamity. Diogo Dalot’s hoofed clearance failed to find Sesko as Luka Vuskovic headed to Gross; Brighton’s captain made room and netted with ease. Even worse followed. Brighton raided along the right, Kostoulas’s cross pinged off Mazraoui’s backside, and there was De Cuyper to finish.

On 72 minutes Carrick played his ace, introducing Fernandes for Mount, then followed up with Cunha. But United remained toothless.

Sports.title: Boehly and Walter sell Chelsea shares as Clearlake Capital takes full control of club
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly and Mark Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea in a deal under which Clearlake Capital takes full control of the Premier League club.

The American billionaire businessmen Boehly and Walter were two of the investors who partnered with Clearlake to buy the club from Roman Abramovich in a sale mandated by the UK government in May 2022. The private equity company Clearlake had previously owned 61.5% of the club, with Boehly and Walter carving up the remaining shares with another investor, Hansjörg Wyss.

A statement issued late on Wednesday night read: “Chelsea Football Club today announced affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, LP will acquire the ownership interest of Todd Boehly. Hansjorg Wyss will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group.

“As part of the transition, Clearlake will also acquire Mark Walter’s ownership interest and therefore acquire full control of the club.”

Chelsea said Boehly, the chair, had shown “unwavering commitment” to the ownership group’s belief that the supporters are at the heart of the club. “The owners have worked together with the shared objective of building a sustainable foundation for long-term sporting success,” the statement added.

“Under their joint ownership, substantial investment has been made across the men’s and women’s senior and youth squads, Chelsea’s training facilities at Cobham, medical and player-support resources, academy development and pathways, and the sporting and business leadership of the club.

“Todd Boehly now leaves his role as chairman with Chelsea well positioned for the next phase of development. Clearlake intends to continue building on the strategic course the club is now on and realising the ambition that the ownership group has developed together.”

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso has been tasked with reviving Chelsea’s fortunes. Photograph: Dave Shopland/AP

Boehly said: “It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club. I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

“I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.”

Behdad Eghbali and José Feliciano, cofounders of Clearlake Capital, said: “Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as chairman. He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family.

“Clearlake has served as Chelsea’s majority owner since 2022, and as we move to full control our focus is to continue investing in the club’s infrastructure, sporting performance, player development and delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the club’s supporters.”

Chelsea, who appointed Xabi Alonso as manager in the summer and are sixth in the Premier League, say there will be no changes to day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club.

Sports.title: Tammy Abraham’s double powers Aston Villa to Carabao Cup win at Coventry
Sports.content:
For Aston Villa, an overdue drama-free outing as Unai Emery’s side cruised into the Carabao Cup fourth round courtesy of a Tammy Abraham double and a Ross Barkley header.

The satisfaction was detectable in Emery’s voice as he reflected on a night of positives: Abraham’s first goals of the season, Ibrahim Mbaye’s encouraging full debut and another half-hour for the £52m club-record signing, Johan Manzambi. Are things clicking into gear after a summer of changes?

Unfortunately for Coventry, it was a sorry case of more of the same. Frank Lampard’s side have lost five of their six matches in all competitions, across which they have leaked 15 goals. It was hard to know whether Abraham’s tap-in or Barkley’s free header, both from corners, was worse from a Coventry perspective. The sight of Lampard hunched in the dugout, hands clasped, has become a familiar sight. “If you give two set pieces away as simply as we did, it’s quite hard to win against Premier League opposition,” the Coventry head coach said.

Lampard’s side, who have lost their opening league four matches by an aggregate of 10-0 and on Saturday visit Nottingham Forest hoping for lift-off, are yet to score outside this competition. Victor Torp’s sweet free-kick from the edge of Villa’s 18-yard box, to cancel out Abraham’s opener, represented Coventry’s first goal since Torp capped the scoring at Plymouth in the previous round. This victory earned Villa a fourth-round trip to Bournemouth at the end of October.

This was the first competitive meeting between these sides since 5 May 2001, when Coventry’s initial 34-year stay in the top flight came to an end with a 3-2 defeat at Villa Park. When Aurèle Amenda limped off with a calf injury after 10 minutes, Bobby Thomas, wearing the captain’s armband, was the only player left of the starting lineup from Sunday’s 5-0 home defeat against Brighton.

Emery made seven changes himself and George Hemmings, one of those to keep their place, was the architect for Villa’s opener. Matteo Ruggeri fed Hemmings down the left and the 19-year-old sent a sumptuous pass into Abraham with the outside of his right boot.

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard shows his disappointment as Coventry suffer another defeat. Photograph: Getty Images/Sportsphoto/Allstar

Coventry struggled to retain possession and Villa were enjoying themselves, exchanging crisp, clean passes. But then Barkley was penalised for fouling Caleb Yirenkyi on the edge of the Villa box and Torp stepped up to lift the subsequent free-kick over the Villa wall. John McGinn, the Villa captain reduced to the role of draught excluder, picked himself up from the turf.

Quick Guide Carabao Cup roundup: Fleetwood handed win over Blades Show A 57th-minute Rhys Norrington-Davies own goal sent Fleetwood into the last 16 of the Carabao Cup for the first time as the League Two club stunned their Championship opponents, Sheffield United, 1-0 at Highbury, before pulling a home tie against Arsenal out in the draw. Matt Lawlor’s side, unbeaten now in nine games in all competitions, had another Danny Andrew effort ruled out for offside and twice hit the woodwork in a dominant second-half display. It was a searching left-wing cross from Andrew that Norrington-Davies nodded beyond Michael Cooper to give the fourth-tier club a historic victory. Tom Cannon did get the ball in the net for Chris Wilder’s visitors who lined up with only four starting survivors from last Friday’s 1-0 league defeat by Wolves. But a flag for offside was raised before the striker slid the ball into the net. United started positively and Ollie Arblaster had a goalbound effort blocked after only 36 seconds. But Mark Helm forced Cooper into a seventh-minute save before the former United forward Ched Evans put his follow-up header narrowly wide. Jay Lynch denied Joe Rothwell as the visitors attacked again but Cooper was the busier, saving from Lewis McCann and Crispin McLean. Helm’s dipping right-foot effort from 18 yards grazed the top netting as Fleetwood finished the first half in the ascendancy and they deserved their break from Norrington-Davies’ own goal. United finally came to life in the last 10 minutes with Lynch brilliantly denied Sydie Peck and Ben Brereton Díaz, while Cannon saw a goalbound strike superbly blocked. Everton’s forgotten man Charly Alcaraz stepped up when his side needed some inspiration to score the only goal in the win over Wolves three minutes after coming on. The Argentinian had played just 14 minutes all season but belied his lack of match sharpness with a quick switch of the ball from one foot to the other to guide a left-footed shot past the former Everton goalkeeper João Virgínia in the 80th minute. It also represented a minor success for Tyler Dibling, whose career has not really taken off since his £35m move from Southampton just over a year ago, as he claimed the assist at the end his most encouraging performance for the club.
