Everton's reward is a home tie against Newcastle. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Suddenly Coventry were full of confidence, a little giddy. Thomas moonlighted as a striker, forcing an error from Tyrone Mings, but then declined a golden opportunity to shoot at goal and the chance fizzled out. Gustavo Hamer then whistled a left-foot shot just past a Villa upright.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Coventry sprung to life but Villa responded. McGinn smacked his hands together after spurning a decent chance and a few minutes later Barkley sent a low drive at goal that Dan Bentley did well to push wide for a corner, from which Villa prospered. Mbaye’s inswinging delivery was on the money and Barkley, totally unmarked in the six-yard box, headed in at the front post.

Coventry had the meanest defence in the Championship last season but have been porous since promotion. More slack marking enabled Villa to extend their lead. McGinn whipped a corner into the six-yard box and Abraham prodded in after walking off his marker, the 18-year-old Coventry debutant Stephen Mfuni, who this month joined on loan from Manchester City.

Abraham’s second gave Villa breathing space. Emery, whose side visit Tottenham on Saturday, felt comfortable enough to withdraw McGinn and Mbaye just after the hour. Zion Suzuki replaced the injured Marco Bizot at half-time, the goalkeeper reporting a back problem. Nicolas Jackson later came on in place of Abraham. Emery cycled through the changes but Alejandro Garnacho, who has played just 31 minutes since signing, remained on the bench.

“He is progressing but we have players in front of him now,” Emery said. “George is playing fantastic, Alysson is understanding a lot of things very good; he needs time but he is giving us things I want. Mbaye responded well. We want a competitive team and the players ready to compete on the standard we have. Of course, he [Garnacho] is a little bit behind because of some circumstances he had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs.”

Sports.title: ‘My scar, not your scar’: Tuchel stands by England semi-final subs but admits wrong timing
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel stands by his heavily criticised defensive substitutions in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina this summer, but the England head coach accepts he made them too early.

Tuchel said England were “waiting for death”, unable to cope with the attacking tactics adopted by Argentina in Atlanta as they chased the game after Anthony Gordon’s opener on the hour. He said fatigue and the success of defending with a back five in knockout games against Mexico and Norway also influenced his decisions to sit on the lead.

That approach proved catastrophic as goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez in the final stages of the game ended England’s dreams of making a first World Cup final since 1966.

“You can try to kill me here. But it’s my scar, it’s not your scar,” Tuchel said in a documentary on the England app. “No one is more hurt than me, no one wanted it more. They can endlessly torture you and think: ‘If I had done different substitutions, then we would have won the match.’ You just don’t know it.

“Of course you could [have made attacking changes]. No one knows what would have happened. We could have done it and maybe lost 2‑1 and could have gone: ‘Is he crazy? He finished the game against Norway with a back five, why didn’t he finish the game with five?’ I think from what I saw and the experience, the information and the level of craziness Argentina put in – change after change after change, it was just one offensive change after the other. That was my solution to the problem.

“That’s what the intervention of a coach is. I try to help, you don’t implement anything for your ego or whatever. You just try to help.”

View image in fullscreen Jordan Pickford is beaten by Enzo Fernández’s shot for Argentina’s first goal. Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/Reuters

England were on the back foot after scoring, with Djed Spence making a last-ditch tackle and Jordan Pickford making a big save immediately before the hydration break. It was then when Tuchel made his ill-fated decision to replace the goalscorer Gordon with the defender Ezri Konsa.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The German, who faced calls to be sacked in the aftermath of the semi-final defeat, insists the opposition’s gung-ho tactics forced his hand. “Argentina then play very, very quickly. Sorry for the language, [they played] fuck-it football: ‘We have nothing to lose. Let’s fuck it.’ A key moment if I look back at it and what happened to my decision-making, we conceded a big, big chance right before the water break. And I thought: ‘We will not survive. This is waiting for death. We don’t have ball possession, we’re not defending good, we’re not defending properly in our 4-4-2. We need help.’

“I changed to a 5-3-2, we changed the structure. Because I believe we can handle the width better and we still have three central defenders in the middle if crosses still fly in. We changed then to a 5-4-1. Even my mindset is maybe like: ‘Let’s just overcome it.’ And it’s too early. Too early for that mindset.”

Sports.title: Enzo Le Fée makes amends from the spot as Sunderland overcome AZ
Sports.content:
Granit Xhaka, Sunderland’s captain, believes it is not unrealistic to dream about Régis Le Bris’s side travelling all the way to the Europa League final next spring.

It is rarely a good idea to dismiss Xhaka but reaching that showpiece in Frankfurt will necessitate considerably more efficient finishing on his team’s part than proved evident on a highly evocative night on Wearside.

Thanks to a second-half penalty from the indefatigable Enzo Le Fée – appropriately the game’s outstanding player – the game ended happily for Sunderland as the home side launched their big return to Europe with a morale-boosting win.

Along the way they missed a litany of chances but, in Le Fée, possessed both a high-calibre attacking playmaker and a tireless off‑the‑ball warrior who, time after time, regained possession for his team.

When Le Bris was invited later to agree that a player he first coached as a 12-year-old in Lorient’s academy was Champions League class, the Sunderland manager’s smile lit up the room. “Enzo’s a great player,” he said. “I trust him and his quality. I’m proud and pleased for the players and the fans, AZ are a really good side but we played with heart and togetherness.”

Occupants of the VIP seats included Jimmy Montgomery, the now 82-year-old hero of Sunderland’s 1973 FA Cup triumph against Leeds and their European goalkeeper during that last, albeit fairly short‑lived, adventure in the Cup Winners’ Cup 53 years ago.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland put on an impressive fireworks display before their European comeback. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

Kick-off was prefaced by a spine-tingling, ear-splitting preamble featuring a giant tifo of a sailing ship floating above the message: “New shores to conquer”.

Not that AZ were inclined to surrender lightly. Leeroy Echteld’s team had enjoyed an unbeaten start to the season, winning five and drawing one of their opening Eredivisie games.

Indeed they would have taken an early lead had Robin Roefs not extended a boot and kept out the dangerous Ro-Zangelo Daal’s low shot after he had been played in by the talented visiting No 10 Kees Smit.

The moment had arrived for Le Fée to start raising the home tone and his half-volley duly tested Jari De Busser. Though De Busser was swiftly forced to push Kevin Danso’s fine shot over the bar, Sunderland almost came undone on the counterattack and it took an excellent interception on Trai Hume’s part to halt Ayoub Oufkir.

Quick Guide Benfica dispatch Amorim's Milan Show Ruben Amorim’s Milan were beaten 2-0 by Marco Silva’s Benfica in the Europa League. Dodi Lukebakio put the Portuguese side ahead at San Siro in the 16th minute and Jakub Kaminski added a second early in the second half. Bayer Leverkusen, finalists in 2024, began their Europa League campaign with a 2-0 win against the Slovenian champions Celje while Lyon were 2-1 winners at Anderlecht. The Cypriot champions Omonia Nicosia stunned the La Liga side Celta Vigo 1-0 while Rangers’ conquerors Jagiellonia Bialystok were denied a point at the Greek giants Olympiacos by Roman Yaremchuk’s late winner. Sparta Prague thrashed Ararat-Armenia 4-1 while Sturm Graz against Rennes and Hapoel Be’er Sheva versus Dinamo Zagreb both ended goalless. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Smit and his teammates issued plenty of reminders that AZ are more than merely deft in possession, but Le Bris’s starting XI was hardly shabby either and, after Wilson Isidor conjured a glorious chance, Le Fée’s shot hit the post.

It was not long before another shot, from Hume this time, whizzed just wide of an upright. When, back in January 2022, Hume joined Sunderland, they were still in League One.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Back in the present Le Bris’s team ended the first half thoroughly dominant yet frustrated. The manager later blamed “overthinking”. Oufkir, meanwhile, was arguably fortunate to collect only a yellow card after sliding in recklessly on Le Fée and was replaced by Weslley Patati at the interval.

AZ re-emerged for the second half invigorated and, as Smit wrong‑footed Sunderland’s rearguard before curling a shot inches wide, it was easy to see why he has collected so many admirers across Europe.

View image in fullscreen Le Fée fires home the decisive penalty. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

Perhaps anxious not to be upstaged, Le Fée swiftly regained the limelight courtesy of a stellar pass that Isidor could not quite polish off.

When Hume subsequently missed another presentable chance it seemed that De Busser’s goal must be protected by some sort of magnetic forcefield.

Then Patati felled Le Fée in the area as he shaped to shoot and a player being scrutinised by the France head coach, Zinedine Zidane, stepped up to the spot.

Having seen a penalty against Arsenal saved expertly by David Raya last Saturday, Le Fée looked a little nervous but he sent De Busser the wrong way as he struck a textbook kick low into the bottom corner. “It was important to score,” Le Bris said. “But Enzo stepped up with bravery and courage. He’s resilient.”

Although Nordi Mukiele and Brian Brobbey, on as a substitute, should really have doubled the lead before Patati’s volley almost provided a late equaliser for AZ, that penalty proved just enough to launch Sunderland’s galleon on European waters.

Sports.title: Saudi Pro League club Al-Taawoun handed stadium ban over Diogo Jota chants
Sports.content:
The Saudi Pro League club Al-Taawoun have been fined nearly £20,000 and given a two-game stadium ban after fans chanted about the late Liverpool and Portugal forward Diogo Jota.

The Al-Hilal midfielder Rúben Neves, who played with Jota for Wolves and Portugal, was shown gesturing to the sky after audible chants of “Jota” from Al-Taawoun fans could be heard during Saturday’s league game.

Jota died in July 2025 along with his brother, André ‌Silva, in a car crash in Spain and Neves was one of the pallbearers at his funeral.

A statement from the Saudi Football Federation read: “The fans of Al-Taawoun chanted phrases and slogans that violated the provisions of the disciplinary and ethics regulations, and the committee decided to increase the penalty in accordance with (39-4) of the disciplinary and ethics regulations.”

The federation ordered Al-Taawoun to play their next two home league matches behind closed doors and fined the club 100,000 riyals (£19,800).

Cristiano Ronaldo, who plays for the rival club Al-Nassr, had called for the fans that chanted about his former international teammate to be punished with stadium lifetime bans.

Sports.title: Raphinha cashes in against Santander with hat-trick as Barça hit seven
Sports.content:
Raphinha scored a hat-trick as Barcelona ripped Racing Santander to shreds in a spectacular 7-2 triumph in La Liga on Wednesday. The win makes Hansi Flick the club’s first manager to win ⁠the opening seven competitive matches of a season.

João Cancelo, Gabriel Jesus and Lamine Yamal also scored for the unstoppable Catalan giants, who have netted 33 goals in those seven games across all competitions, and who moved three points clear of Real Madrid at the top of La Liga.

With lightning flashing above the Camp Nou, Barça started at rapid pace and took the lead with a thunderbolt from Cancelo. The defender crashed a shot in off the crossbar from long range in the eighth minute.

View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal celebrates scoring Barcelona’s seventh goal. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters

Dani Olmo twice came close before Raphinha won and converted a penalty for Barça’s second. The Brazilian was clumsily brought down by Pedro Felipe and thrashed the spot-kick into the bottom right corner.

Santander pulled one back when Maguette Gueye barged his way through and produced a neat finish to beat Joan García in goal. However, it proved only brief respite, with Cancelo provoking the third with another long-range effort which deflected in off Asier Villalibre.

Raphinha, thriving playing as a centre-forward, bagged Barça’s fourth after he was played in on goal by Olmo. Lamine Yamal should have added a fifth after the electric Karim Adeyemi was brought down in the box, but Julen Agirrezabala saved his penalty.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barça’s reserve goalkeeper Wojciech Szczesny replaced García at half-time after the Spain international appeared to hurt himself while slipping as he went to get the ball. Lamine Yamal hit a post and later had a goal ruled out for offside, as the youngster suffered a more frustrating night than some of his colleagues.

In the second half Yassir Zabiri pulled another back for Santander after a dreadful error from Szczesny, who tried and failed to dribble the ball. Zabiri tackled him to score.

Barcelona’s fifth arrived almost immediately with another penalty after Adeyemi was brought down. Raphinha completed his hat-trick from the spot for his ninth league goal, extending his lead as the league’s top goalscorer.

He was replaced by his compatriot Gabriel Jesus, who added the sixth with a sharp finish into the top corner after being played in by Lamine Yamal. The winger eventually got his goal when Adeyemi roared down the left wing and set him up for Barça’s seventh and final goal.

Atlético Madrid warmed up for Saturday’s derby with Real with a 4-0 home win over Osasuna. Jonathan David, Lee Kang-in, Robin Le Normand and Alex Baena were on target in a one-sided contest at the Metropolitano as Diego Simeone’s side moved into third, five points behind Barcelona.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Madrid endure an awkward night after T-shirt trouble and Elche scare
Sports.content:
REAL UNEASE

Anxious to sample some traditional Spanish culture while taking in a La Liga match years ago, Football Daily and some friends decamped to Gran Alicant. As we prepared to leave a quaint bodega (the Dick Turpin), where we’d been sampling the local hooch (Guinness), to travel to the nearby stadium, an elderly local resident with an unmistakable mackem accent informed us that the Elche home game to which we were heading was not being played until the following evening. It had fallen victim to Spanish TV’s infuriating habit of rescheduling random top-flight matches with little or no notice or consideration for Johnny-come-latelys who might have travelled from afar to watch them. We never did get to see Elche play in the flesh but did get to watch the current La Liga basement-dwellers give José Mourinho an almighty fright on TV on Tuesday night, as they went this close to snatching a point from Real Madrid.

Allowed to spend 14 times more on players and coaching staff than their hosts at the Estadio Martínez Valero under La Liga rules, it was no surprise to see Real Madrid go 2-0 up as they appeared to be cruising towards a routine rout of their lowly opposition. However, a succession of missed chances (hello, Vinícius Júnior) followed by second-half sucker punches from Abiel Osorio and Fer Niño meant Mourinho was sweating as Elche approached the final seven minutes on the front foot, looking for an unlikely winner. Sadly, there was no fairytale and Carlos Espí popped up with a late, late winner to break Elche hearts and dig his side out of one of several holes they have already found themselves in this season. While a balmy Tuesday night in Elche may not be the most glamorous of environments, not for the first, second, third, fourth or even 534th time in their history, Madrid found a way.

“Three points and nothing more,” harrumphed Mourinho in his post-match interview. “The problem seems obvious to me. It’s harder to know why but it’s easier to understand that there are matches that seem over but in the end, aren’t. Matches where we have three, four, five chances to finish them but don’t. After failing to do so, it feels like we go from ease to losing control. With the changes I made in the end, I took all the risks. We won but I could have lost.” Modest to a T, as ever, Mourinho will be hoping for a better performance from his team when they make the short trip to the Wanda Metropolitano to face their city rivals Atlético on Sunday (or Saturday, depending on the whims of broadcasters) before the international break.

While the out-of-sorts Vinícius Jr did little on Tuesday night beyond convince Arsenal fans they may have dodged a very expensive summer bullet, he was one of three Madrid stars who refused to show off T-shirts showing solidarity with the people of Ceuta that were handed to both sets of players as they made their way out on to the pitch before kick-off. Along with Kylian Mbappé and Ibrahima Konaté, Vinícius Jr chose not to show the slogan “Todos somos caballas” (“We are all mackerels”), in support of the Spanish exclave which was overwhelmed by the arrival of 80,000 migrants, mostly from Morocco, in recent months. Subsequently lambasted in some quarters for being too supportive of the migrants and not supportive enough of the citizens of Ceuta, it was an awkward situation where the Madrid players were put on the spot and simply couldn’t do right for doing wrong.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Niall McVeigh at 8pm (BST) for a red-hot Bigger Vase clockwatch, while Will Unwin will be on deck at the same time for Rumblews Cup goal updates.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote, ‘I regret that I didn’t eat some grass after the match to keep something from this in my body forever’. That was the feeling. That was the moment” – as part of the FA’s forthcoming feature ‘Reflections: England’s World Cup Journey’, Thomas Tuchel was recently interviewed by Daniel Sturridge about the aftermath of England’s famous 3-2 win over Mexico at the Azteca, and made a bizarre admission about his eating habits while showing an alarming misunderstanding of the body’s digestive system.

View image in fullscreen Thomas Tuchel failed to mention what he was chewing during that second half with Argentina. Photograph: Ricardo Mazalán/AP

double quotation mark I almost wish I was a West Ham fan. As an eternally suffering Spurs supporter, I find myself looking enviously towards the London Stadium these days. The Hammers are top of the table, banging in goal after goal (already 20 more than Spurs’ tally in the league). They score even when they lose and seem to have bought a proper No 9. My Spurs, meanwhile, continue the tradition of the last two years in style, sitting comfortably in 17th with 1,047 wingers on contract, and getting knocked out of one of the competitions they could ‘conceivably’ have won, the only competition they seem to be able to score goals in as well. In hindsight, West Ham made the right choice to go down. Hammers fans, you are welcome!” – Yannick Woudstra (and no others).

double quotation mark Hugh Fordham’s idea [Tuesday’s Football Daily letters] has some merit. But it reminded me of a pithy comment by Bill Nicholson. ‘Do you think he was interfering with play?’, he was asked. Nicholson responded: “If he’s not interfering with play, what’s he doing on the pitch?!’” – Harry McDonald.

double quotation mark In support of Hugh Fordham’s suggestion, I remember discussing the idea of interfering with play while on a training course for referees back in the 1960s. We were told that unless someone was ‘lying injured near the corner flag’ any player should be treated as being involved in play. Not a lot of room for subjectivity in those days. And obviously no thought of stopping play for the hypothetical injured player!” – Trevor Field.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Harry McDonald. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Dejected Michael Carrick hits out at 'unacceptable' Man United performance after dismal Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton as he breaks silence on JJ Gabriel, 15, after wonderkid's quit threat
Sports.content:
Dejected Michael Carrick hits out at 'unacceptable' Man United performance after dismal Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton as he breaks silence on JJ Gabriel, 15, after wonderkid's quit threat

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Carrick insists he is not feeling the pressure as Manchester United manager after an 'unacceptable' Carabao Cup exit at the hands of Brighton.

Carrick and his plays were booed off with chants of 'what the f***ing hell was that?' from the displeased supporters in the Stretford End after United blew a 2-0 lead to lose 3-2.

'We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it,' Carrick said.

'The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me.

'We'll all be better. We have to be better. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We're out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches. It doesn't feel good at the moment.'

Director of football Jason Wilcox looked shellshocked at the final whistle and after throwing away victory in the final seconds at Everton, losing in abject fashion at Old Trafford to Manchester City and now getting out-worked at home by Brighton to go out of the cup, the boos of discontent are growing ever louder.

Michael Carrick says it's not acceptable to see his Man United side tumble out the Carabao Cup

Carrick saw his United side blow a 2-0 lead to lose 3-2 at Old Trafford against Brighton

'We all know it's there,' Carrick said of the boos.

'We know it's there whether it's good or whether it's not good. I think it's pretty obvious.

'We've all got feelings, we've all got emotions to a point, but it's how you deal with that that is the important thing. Being here toughens you up over a period of time, so it depends how you deal with it.

'You've got to deal with it in a way where you can cope with it and you can bring out the best in yourself, and whatever, however you do that, with your motivation and the confidence deep within yourself, as a whole group I'm talking about here, that we know we can win football matches and that's what we are here for is to win.'

Asked if this miserable start to the season, which also saw United lose at newly-promoted Hull City on the opening weekend, has him sweating over his job, Carrick was defiant in response.

'No, I don't feel under pressure,' he said.

'Either way, that doesn't bother me one bit. It generally doesn't bother me one bit.

'I understand what goes on outside and how the world works, but it generally doesn't bother me.

'What bothers me is winning games and having a good feeling around the place, and a good feeling around the group to know we're moving in a good direction. That's ultimately what bothers me.

'When we're on a good run, the biggest thing I'm worried about or thinking about is keeping the good run going and keeping everything on an even level really, to keep pushing that it's not enough.

'And if we're not on a good run, then we've got to get back to being on a good run. So, that's as simple as it gets.

'We've got to win football matches and we can do; I fully believe we will do. But obviously we've got to do it pretty quick and Sunday is a starting point.'

Shea Lacey scored the opening goal – a 'great moment' that Carrick conceded will get lost in light of this cup exit – and Mason Mount added a second before United unravelled badly.

But it was another academy player, 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, that dominated the lead-up to this match after the youngster, along with his family, requested contract termination as he shocked everyone at the club by asking to leave.

Join the discussion What does Man United need more right now: stronger leadership or better support for young talent?

Manchester United's teenage prodigy JJ Gabriel, 15, announced on Tuesday that he wants out

Gabriel's entourage have been left displeased by his lack of first team opportunities and while the original plan was to include him in the matchday squad for the Brighton game, that had to be shelved following the termination request and the fact Gabriel has not trained this week as he now appears to be effectively on strike.

'I just think we've got to be really careful of the whole situation,' Carrick said of Gabriel's situation.

'He's a young boy, he's 15, and for me, definitely, and from a club point of view, is about looking after our younger players, their welfare, their well-being, their exposure, and I think we've got to be really, all of us, I think we've got to be really conscious of that in this situation,' Carrick added.

Asked if he is involved in ongoing conversations given United still feel this situation with their brightest attacking player is rectifiable, Carrick confirmed it's a team effort.

'As a club for sure, we're all involved in those conversations,' he concluded. 'I just think we've got to be very careful of that.'

Brighton never lost belief and that was the key ingredient that they had against United to come from 2-0 down to win 3-2, according to their boss Fabian Hurzeler.

'I definitely believed and belief was a big word in the preparation for us,' he explained.

'When you go to a place like here you need to have belief and then to show it when you are 2-0 down shows real character.

'That shows the players have a real social bond.

'The foundation was that togetherness, this connection, the relationships they build on the pitch. The longer the game went on the more we had control.'

Sports.title: Three Man City kids who can light up the Carabao Cup: The one-on-one dribbler who has blown Enzo Maresca away, the defender who took up boxing to toughen up and the 6ft midfield goal-machine with an unlikely first-team buddy
Sports.content:
During his first weeks in the job at Manchester City, Enzo Maresca revealed three academy kids had impressed him sufficiently to earn a permanent residence in first-team training this season.

Ryan McAidoo, Kaden Braithwaite and Floyd Samba were the trio who stood out more than the rest on the pre-season tour of Asia, with Maresca’s staff devising plans to divide the players’ time between the senior group and getting minutes for the Under 21s.

Both McAidoo and Braithwaite have already featured in the Premier League, with Samba on the hunt for a senior debut when City face Norwich City in the Carabao Cup tonight.

‘When we started pre-season we had many young players, and then at the end we decided to keep these three because we think they can improve training with us and then they can get some minutes,’ Maresca said.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the journey all three have taken so far at the Etihad Stadium.

RYAN McAIDOO

Age: 18, Position: Right winger

Maresca was blown away by McAidoo’s ability one-on-one during his first few sessions in Asia, with the winger stealing the show in a friendly against Inter.

A shoulder injury curtailed the start of his season but the 18-year-old is set for minutes having come off the bench in the Premier League against Crystal Palace and Coventry City.

Ryan McAidoo of Manchester City in action against Coventry City this season. The 18-year-old right winger is a wonderful dribbler and superb in one-on-one situations

McAidoo, who joined City from Chelsea two years ago, is considered the jewel of those breaking through at the Etihad

Considered the jewel of those breaking through at City, McAidoo joined from Chelsea two years ago – and scored on his senior debut in January, a 10-1 win over Exeter City in the FA Cup.

He was the first transfer between City and Chelsea at academy level since an informal pact between former director Jason Wilcox and his counterpart Neil Bath down at Cobham, struck so neither club would target the other’s teenage talents.

McAidoo’s journey at City has so far been stable, scoring 10 goals in 19 Under-18 league games in his opening year. Asked by Daily Mail Sport if the year had surprised him, he said: ‘No, not really. I’d planned it to go well but not this well.’

So there is a quiet confidence about a youngster whose progress England’s Under 21s are tracking and who has benefited from individual one-to-one coaching at club level.

His first training session with Pep Guardiola came at 16. Coaches were keen to work on his decision-making during the private work away from the group. They worked on timing when to cross rather than relying on dribbling past markers – even if McAidoo is devastating at that, still the clear elite facet of his game.

His coach, Oliver Reiss, even set targets of how many crosses to attempt in certain games as City attempted to challenge somebody who could find matches too easy.

McAidoo scored a 19-minute hat-trick off the bench in the UEFA Youth League against Feyenoord as a central striker while barely having completed his GCSEs and then stepped up to the higher age group last year, combining that with more consistent first-team training call-ups.

Notably the number of assists went up, which indicates McAidoo has taken on board the advice around decisions in the box. Sources say the next part to target is his movement and knowing when to attack the back post.

‘One of the surprises has been Ryan McAidoo, which nobody expected,’ Maresca said recently. ‘He was very good. I really like players who are aggressive in wide areas.

‘For him the best thing is to learn. Try to be intelligent, try to learn from Antoine (Semenyo) and Jeremy (Doku). When I say try to learn, it’s not in terms of how to dribble – it’s about working hard because it can be difficult with young players, they can stop working because they feel they are ready when they are not.’

Enzo Maresca is full of praise for McAidoo. 'I really like players who are aggressive in wide areas,' the manager said recently of the 18-year-old

McAidoo in action on his senior debut in January, a 10-1 win over Exeter City in the FA Cup in which he scored

KADEN BRAITHWAITE

Age: 18, Position: Central defender

Captain of the FA Youth Cup-winning team last season, Braithwaite officially joined City at the age of eight and is in a long line of academy products who have gone right through the ranks.

Braithwaite was part of the backline that kept JJ Gabriel quiet in that final against Manchester United in May and had already made his first-team bow by that point.

It was in the Carabao Cup third round two years ago when Braithwaite became the third-youngest player in the club’s history, starting the 2-1 victory over Watford. Only Glyn Pardoe and Paul Simpson made debuts younger than the then-16-year-old.

Interestingly, there were staff at the time who felt that Stephen Mfuni – now on loan at Coventry City for the season – was ahead of Braithwaite in the pecking order. The pair are the same age, born four days apart in February 2008, but Braithwaite’s first session with Guardiola’s squad two days out from that tie convinced the Catalan to throw him in at the deep end.

As with McAidoo, Braithwaite is set individual targets by coaches. At 16, it was to win more duels.

The Bolton-born teenager then took up boxing in a bid to toughen up – claiming that he had previously been too nice – and has caught the eye of Maresca with his composure and additional strength, making his Premier League debut against Palace last month.

Kaden Braithwaite was captain of the FA Youth Cup-winning Manchester City team last season and part of the backline that kept Manchester United's JJ Gabriel quiet

In the Carabao Cup third round two years ago, Braithwaite became the third-youngest player in Manchester City's history, starting the 2-1 victory over Watford

FLOYD SAMBA

Age: 17, Position: Central midfielder

Scorer of a sublime 25-yard curling free-kick in the FA Youth Cup final last season and has an eye for goal when breaking into the box from midfield.

He has netted a goal a game in the league for the Under 21s and Under 18s over the past year and at 6ft, already looks a commanding presence. In all, he contributed 24 goals and 10 assists in 38 appearances last season.

Samba’s brother Tyrone (18) regularly plays in the same team, while their younger brother Emerson is also a promising central defender within City’s academy.

Floyd Samba has been in Manchester City’s youth set-up throughout his childhood and has consistently excelled through the age groups

Samba scored a sublime free-kick in last season's FA Youth Cup final against Manchester United

The surname might feel familiar, with Samba the son of former Blackburn Rovers and Queens Park Rangers defender Chris.

Like Braithwaite, Samba has also been in City’s youth set-up throughout his childhood. Long-serving scout Mike Hayes spotted him at the Wilmslow Football Academy, a place specialising in summer soccer camps, and he has since consistently excelled through the age groups.

Fast forward to today, and Samba has taken on a surprising mentor within the first-team building.

Despite not yet mastering English and coming across as almost painfully shy, Uzbek Abdukodir Khusanov has been the one (alongside Gianluigi Donnarumma) who is helping Samba settle.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly LEAVES Chelsea: Behdad Eghbali's Clearlake Capital complete £1bn deal to buy minority owner's stake in the club as they take 'full control'
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly LEAVES Chelsea: Behdad Eghbali's Clearlake Capital complete £1bn deal to buy minority owner's stake in the club as they take 'full control'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Behdad Eghbali and his Clearlake Capital group have taken full control of Chelsea after purchasing Todd Boehly and Mark Walter's minority shares in the club.

Boehly, Walter and Hansjorg Wyss owned 38.5 per cent of the Premier League side collectively. The other 61.5 per cent was held by Clearlake, who are led by Eghbali and Jose E Feliciano.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that a sale process was ongoing and Clearlake Capital have now bought out Boehly and Walter in a deal that is believed to be worth around £1billion. Wyss has not sold his shares and is remaining part of the ownership, however.

In a statement, the club said: 'Chelsea Football Club today announced affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, L.P. (“Clearlake”) will acquire the ownership interest of Todd Boehly. Hansjorg Wyss will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group.

'As part of the transition, Clearlake will also acquire Mark Walter’s ownership interest and therefore acquire full control of the club.'

Clearlake have financed the purchase itself, with Eghbali and Feliciano - who hailed Boehly as 'an important partner' - said to have put forward large investments.

Todd Boehly has sold his minority stake in Chelsea to Behdad Eghbali's Clearlake Capital Group

Boehly's fellow minority owner Mark Walter has also sold his shares (pictured - Boehly with Eghbali in 2025)

In their statement, Chelsea added: 'In 2022, Todd Boehly and Clearlake joined together to lead the historic acquisition of Chelsea – successfully navigating an unprecedented period of uncertainty imposed by outside political events – and Todd organised his chairmanship with an unwavering commitment to this ownership group’s fundamental belief that the supporters are at the heart of everything the club does.

'The owners have worked together with the shared objective of building a sustainable foundation for long-term sporting success.

'Under their joint-ownership, substantial investment has been made across the men's and women's senior and youth squads, Chelsea’s training facilities at Cobham, medical and player-support resources, academy development and pathways, and the sporting and business leadership of the club.

'Todd Boehly now leaves his role as chairman with Chelsea well positioned for the next phase of development. The progress made over the past four years reflects the shared commitment of Clearlake, Boehly and the wider ownership group and the leadership, staff, coaches and players at Chelsea.

'Clearlake intends to continue building on the strategic course the club is now on and realising the ambition that the ownership group has developed together.'

Boehly said: 'It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club. I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

'I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.'

While Boehly was Chelsea chairman and was the original face of the 2022 takeover, Eghbali has been the most hands-on of all the co-owners. He often liaises with the sporting directorship team and is a consistent attendee at games both at home and away.

In a statement issued to Bloomberg last week, a spokesperson for Walter confirmed that he was seeking a sale with an agreement close.

Daily Mail Sport had also reported that the pair were expecting to make a minor profit on their original investment.The entire consortium purchased Chelsea for £2.5billion in 2022 with an additional £1.75bn committed to investment in the club.

Boehly tried his hand at being involved in transfers early on – he once admitted to buying Marc Cucurella from Brighton because Manchester City also wanted him – though Eghbali has largely led the show since that early experiment.

Reports have suggested Boehly and Eghbali held a strained relationship and there had been speculation surrounding one buying out the other for around two years now.

Sports.title: These are desperate days for Man United: After derby defeat and academy star JJ Gabriel's public snub, it gets even worse for Michael Carrick as Brighton fight back to knock them out of the Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
What desperate days these are for Manchester United. Beaten here in the Old Trafford derby on Sunday, at odds with supporters and in danger of losing the crown jewel of their academy, they crashed out of the Carabao Cup at the first attempt for the second year in a row. At least Brighton aren’t Grimsby.

The night had started so positively as well. Leading 2-0 inside 10 minutes, United looked to be cruising into the fourth round. Better still, the scorer of the first goal on his first start was teenager Shea Lacey who couldn’t have timed it more perfectly following the bombshell news on Tuesday that his Under-21s teammate JJ Gabriel wants to quit the club.

But it has been a poor start to the new season for Michael Carrick’s side, and it was about to get even worse as Brighton fought back to stun Old Trafford with their fifth win here in six visits.

It was also the first time in 50 years and 146 games that United have lost at home after being two goals ahead, going back to a 3-2 defeat to Tottenham in September, and the first after leading at half-time since Ipswich won here in 1984.

After a tame defeat in the derby to Manchester City on Sunday that could not be hidden behind the VAR controversy over Erling Haaland’s winning goal, this was a second defeat in four days at Old Trafford.

The boos at full-time told their own story. Carrick takes his team to Fulham on Sunday knowing that another one will put him under close early-season scrutiny going into the long international break.

Maxim De Cuyper wheels away in celebration after scoring Brighton's winner vs Man United

Michael Carrick saw his United side lose a 2-0 lead to get knocked out of the Carabao Cup

It's been a tumultuous few days for the Red Devils on and off the field and this only adds to it

‘We can't accept that as a group,’ said the United boss. ‘I take responsibility for it. It's on me ultimately. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.

‘The pressure doesn’t bother me one bit. I understand how the world works. The feeling at the start of the game to the feeling at the end couldn’t be further apart. It’s happened so quickly over two or three weeks, there’s a lot of disappointment.

‘Of course we can turn it around. We have to be better. It doesn't feel good at the moment. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to go back to winning football matches.’

On the furore over Gabriel, Carrick added: ‘We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy. It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really.’

The news about Gabriel could hardly have come at a worse time. Lacey appeared to react to it on Tuesday night by posting a photo of himself walking into Old Trafford along with a heart emoji, and he made another point inside eight minutes when he fired United ahead.

It was a particularly sweet moment for the 19-year-old given that he was sent off against Brighton on his home debut as a substitute in January.

There was something inevitable about his goal last night. Youri Tielemans picked out Lacey on the right side of the box and he cut inside Jaouen Hadjam before whipping a shot inside Jason Steele’s near post.

Old Trafford rose to salute the first teenager to score on his United debut since Marcus Rashford against Midtjylland here a decade ago.

The fans had only just settled down when Mason Mount had them off their seats again in the 10 minute. Rashford picked Costinha’s pocket and breezed past Luka Vuskovic. Steele kept out his effort but the ball ran to Mount who got there just ahead of Lacey to score the second.

Shea Lacey kisses the Manchester United badge after opening the scoring in the match

United doubled their lead on 10 minutes when Mason Mount scored with this right-footed shot

Charalampos Kostoulas started the Brighton comeback with this shot just before half-time

Pascal Gross (second right) levelled the scoreline for the Seagulls with this left-footed finish

At that stage, who could have foreseen the pain that was about to follow?

United were enjoying themselves and the crowd loved it when Rashford, who had Costinha on the run down the left, nutmegged Chema Andres.

But there was a vulnerability to them that was perhaps epitomised by the young centre-back partnership of Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro after Carrick made eight changes from the derby and waited too long to change back again as the tide of the game turned dramatically against his team.

‘The performance towards the end of the first half is on me,’ he admitted after Brighton took control of the game and threatened on a number of occasions before Charalampos Kostoulas pulled a goal back in added time at end of the half.

United were unhappy that referee Farai Hallam didn’t give Benjamin Sesko a free kick when he was floored by a tag team of Malick Yalcouye and Olivier Boscagli, but they switched off as Hadjam’s long diagonal pass picked out Kostoulas who got in between Heaven and Darlow to score.

The equaliser arrived in the 64th minute when Diogo Dalot hooked a clearance towards halfway where Sesko was under pressure by Pascal Struijk and succeeded only in heading the ball 30 yards back towards his own goal. Pascal Gross was waiting to receive it on the edge of the box and sold Yoro a dummy before sliding a shot past Darlow.

The momentum was with Brighton and Kostoulas got away from Mazraoui in the 69th minute and crossed for substitute Maxim De Cuyper to complete an incredible comeback.

‘I definitely believed and belief was a big word in the preparation for us,’ said head coach Fabian Hurzeler. ‘When you go to a place like this you need to have belief and then to show it when you are two goals down shows real character.’

Sports.title: Liverpool to face Chelsea in blockbuster Xabi Alonso homecoming as Arsenal travel to League Two minnows and Everton host Newcastle: CARABAO CUP FOURTH-ROUND DRAW
Sports.content:
Liverpool to face Chelsea in blockbuster Xabi Alonso homecoming as Arsenal travel to League Two minnows and Everton host Newcastle: CARABAO CUP FOURTH-ROUND DRAW

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool will entertain Chelsea in a blockbuster all-Premier League encounter in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

The clash, the pick of the ties in Wednesday's draw, will see former Reds midfielder Xabi Alonso return to Anfield for the first time since taking over at Stamford Bridge.

Elsewhere, Arsenal will travel to League Two side Fleetwood Town, who are in the fourth round for the first time in their history after beating Sheffield United 1-0.

Fleetwood are the lowest-ranked side left in the competition and play at the aptly-named Highbury Stadium.

The Gunners, last season's beaten finalists, thumped Ipswich 4-2 on Tuesday night.

Holders Manchester City play their third round tie against Norwich City on Thursday, and the victor of that match is set to entertain Brighton.

Liverpool will entertain Chelsea in the pick of the Carabao Cup fourth-round ties

Sunderland were drawn at home to Brentford in one of several encounters between top flight clubs, while Crystal Palace were rewarded for beating Middlesbrough last week with an away game at Fulham.

Everton, searching for their first major trophy since 1995, will play Newcastle, who won the Carabao Cup in 2024-25, at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Bournemouth have been handed a home tie against Aston Villa after Unai Emery's side picked up their first domestic victory of the season at Coventry on Wednesday via a 3-1 triumph.

Bradford City and Peterborough are the only two League One representatives still in the competition and they have been drawn against each other, with the Bantams set to host that game.

The fourth round matches will all be played in the week commencing October 26, rather than being split over two weeks like the third round was.

Everton, Fleetwood, Villa and Brighton were all winners on Wednesday night, with the Seagulls coming from 2-0 down to beat Man United 3-2 at Old Trafford in the biggest shock of the round.

Sports.title: Aston Villa heap misery on Frank Lampard's Coventry with 3-1 Carabao Cup victory... it's early days but this season is already looking alarming for the Sky Blues, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Aston Villa heap misery on Frank Lampard's Coventry with 3-1 Carabao Cup victory... it's early days but this season is already looking alarming for the Sky Blues, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Frank Lampard is learning that even when you lead a club to promotion, management can feel a horribly lonely place when it starts to go wrong.

The former England midfielder guided Coventry back to the top flight for the first time in 25 years but just six games into their campaign, it is already looking alarming. Their defending was awful here, particularly from set pieces, and there were some boos in the second half.

‘When you concede simple goals like we did from set pieces, it’s hard to win against Premier League opposition,’ Lampard said. ‘It’s mentally difficult for players. The soft nature of the second and third goals meant it wasn’t easy to come back.’

The Carabao Cup will not determine Coventry’s season. However, they have now lost five of six in all competitions as Aston Villa claimed their first victory in domestic football this term. Two goals from Tammy Abraham – who was given his chance by Lampard at Chelsea – and another from Ross Barkley sent Villa into round five, with Victor Torp’s first-half equaliser a rare bright moment for Lampard’s team.

Villa boss Unai Emery will be encouraged by Ibrahim Mbaye’s exciting performance, which could earn him a starting spot at Tottenham on Saturday. Villa made seven changes to Coventry’s nine, and both conceded far too many chances. However, there was still no place for Alejandro Garnacho, who has played just 31 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea.

Tammy Abraham scored twice as Aston Villa beat Coventry City 3-1 in the EFL Cup third round

Unai Emery wanted Abraham to leave this summer, but the striker silenced the doubters here

It was another brutal result for Frank Lampard and his side must dramatically and quickly

‘It’s about working and training,’ said Emery. ‘When he has minutes to play, he must try and play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now.’

Emery was not thrilled that Abraham decided to stay at Villa rather than join Ipswich on loan and in the early exchanges, the Villa boss berated his forward twice for failing to follow instructions.

Abraham answered in the best way possible. George Hemmings collected a pass from full debutant Matteo Ruggeri and slipped Abraham through for a calm finish beyond Dan Bentley.

Villa looked in control until Barkley trod on the ball and fouled Caleb Yirenkyi just outside the Villa box. From the free-kick, Torp curled in Coventry’s first home goal of the season.

Last time these clubs met, in 2001, Coventry lost 3-2 at Villa Park and were relegated from the top flight. They have been all the way to League Two and back since then and the equaliser made them believe once more.

Bobby Thomas robbed Tyrone Mings inside the box but instead of shooting, tried to tee up Sidiki Cherif for a debut goal. Then Gustavo Hamer’s dipping effort flew just wide.

Neither side’s defence was remotely convincing and Ibrahim Mbaye was enjoying his first start for Villa. The £50m signing’s shot rebounded into the path of John McGinn who shot wide, before Barkley went close from 25 yards.

Bentley tipped that one wide but from Mbaye’s corner, Barkley was left alone on the edge of the six-yard box to head Emery’s men back in front.

There was still time before the break for Cherif to shoot straight at Marco Bizot when he should have picked out a team-mate. That would be reserve keeper Bizot’s last involvement as he was replaced by Zion Suzuki for the second half.

If Coventry’s marking was bad for the second goal, they surpassed themselves for the third. This time McGinn drilled a low bar that was dummied by Barkley and Hemmings and steered home by Abraham inside the six-yard box. Not one of the Sky Blues players inside the box had attempted a clearance.

Sports.title: Enzo Le Fee's magic lit up the Stadium of Light to inspire Sunderland to an unforgettable 1-0 win over AZ Alkmaar - and the Black Cats showed why they belong in Europe, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
He arrived in the Championship but is deserving of the Champions League. For now at least, Enzo Le Fee is the reason Sunderland are playing, and winning, in the Europa League.

Just when this big occasion demanded a big player to conjure a big moment, the little magician from Brittany reached into his bag of tricks, bamboozled AZ Alkmaar’s defenders and cast a spell over a home crowd that will last a lifetime. They will not forget this night.

It was in the 65th minute that Le Fee won and then converted the penalty that meant Sunderland’s first European fixture in 53 years ended in a deserved victory. No player deserved that place in the history books more than him. He had illuminated the Stadium of Light long before his goal, just like he did last season. The 26-year-old, once of Roma, is a special, special player. He, just like the occasion, did not disappoint.

‘You need good players in the right moment,’ said Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris. ‘And Enzo is a great player. He can create, he can score, he can help in defence. Yes, he’s great!’

Sunderland’s stadium took its name from one of European football’s greatest venues, Benfica’s Estadio da Luz. Opened in 1997 with the dream of continental nights like this, as recently as five years ago there was not so much light as the darkness of League One. It was Accrington, not Alkmaar. Morecambe, not Milan.

Enzo Le Fee coolly converted his second-half spot-kick to earn Sunderland a mighty 1-0 win

His penalty earned Sunderland victory over AZ Alkmaar in their first European game since 1974

MATCH FACTS Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 8; Mukiele 7, Danso 7, Alderete 6 (Ballard 52, 7), Reinildo 6; Xhaka 7, Sadiki 6; Hume 7, Le Fee 9, Fofana 5 (Angulo 67, 6); Isidor 6 (Brobbey 67, 6) Subs: Moore, Ballard, Methalie, Rigg, Meunier, O'Nien, Ahoka, Jones, Tutierov, Proctor Manager: Regis Le Bris 6 Referee: J Pignard (FRA) 7 Man of the Match : Le Fee

But this is not the story of a plucky underdog, dining at a table at which they do not really belong. Sunderland should be playing in Europe. Sunderland should wave their flags and plant them loudly and proudly on foreign soil this autumn. Come spring, Sunderland should still be in this competition. They’re here not by winning a cup - as they last were in 1973 - but by finishing seventh in the world’s strongest league.

This game was not really about the result, either. It was about ‘I was there’, and I want to be here again. Half a century and more is a long time between European nights. The last one came at Roker Park, against Sporting Lisbon, in a competition that no longer exists. There are supporters here who have lived through an entire generation between continental visitors. For others, this was the first taste, sight and smell of something they had only ever watched and imagined happening elsewhere. For the majority, this was not European football coming back to Wearside, it was the arrival of it.

That was certainly the pervading feeling among those on the playing side. Le Bris and captain Granit Xhaka have been singing from the same hymn sheet this week, chorusing the message that this is just the start, not the final destination. It was, however, never going to be an understated opening to this chapter.

The guttural release when the teams emerged, the same raw sound when League One survivor Trai Hume took out Ayoub Oufkir and the giddy shrieks of the barely believable when Le Fee almost scored direct from an early corner all ensured that the action on the pitch satisfied the anticipation in the stands. This was good. Great, even. Sunderland were playing in Europe, and they were playing well.

Defender Kevin Danso, scorer of one League Cup goal in three years at Tottenham, went in search of the Puskas Award with a 25-yard dipper tipped over by Jari De Busser. Le Fee’s shot then tested the base of the post and this stadium’s plastic seating, given the 48,000 who crashed back into theirs in despair. Or maybe that’s the wrong word, because there was nothing despairing about Sunderland’s performance.

But Alkmaar were good, too. That helped. This felt proper. Loaded with academy products, we will no doubt see the likes of midfielder Kees Smit and forward Ro-Zangelo Daal in the Premier League at some point, even if at inflated fees. Maybe Sunderland, of Europe, will be shopping in that market.

To get here, their recruitment has been rather more shrewd. Take Xhaka. Rarely will £17m be better spent on a player north of 30 years old. To the left of him, on the wing, was a team-mate who could represent the future direction, £31m deadline-day signing Malick Fofana. Not that the Belgium international, 21, appears on the same page as his colleagues just yet.

The page-turner, rather, was Le Fee.

The spirited Black Cats proved why they belong back in Europe on an unforgettable night

There was, though, a period around the hour that was something of a European tutorial for the home side. Their energy, understandably, had faded. AZ took charge, teasing and weaving passes and patterns. How would Sunderland respond? Well, give the ball to Le Fee, of course.

And so, in the 64th minute, he weaved a pattern of his own, right through the penalty area. Just as he was about to shoot, he was tripped. Penalty. He missed last weekend against Arsenal. He was not missing this one.

Sports.title: Man United 2-3 Brighton PLAYER RATINGS: Which player endured a 'very difficult night'? Who did himself no favours after falling down the pecking order - and which three stars disappointed with 4/10 displays?
Sports.content:
Man United 2-3 Brighton PLAYER RATINGS: Which player endured a 'very difficult night'? Who did himself no favours after falling down the pecking order - and which three stars disappointed with 4/10 displays?

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United crashed out of the Carabao Cup as boos rang out at Old Trafford on another damaging night for Michael Carrick.

Brighton were 2-0 down and reeling 10 minutes in after goals from Shea Lacey, marking his first start, and Mason Mount.

United had never lost from the previous 145 games when 2-0 up at Old Trafford but there was a nervousness in the air, not least when Charalampos Kostoulas made it 2-1 just before half-time.

Carrick's side never got a grip on this topsy-turvy game thereafter and goals from Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper condemned United to a Carabao Cup exit at the first attempt for the second successive season.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT gives his verdict on Carrick's charges as they bow out of the Carabao Cup…

Brighton produced yet another emphatic performance here at Old Trafford in the Carabao Cup

Michael Carrick looked furious on the touchline at the end as Manchester United crashed out

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1)

Karl Darlow – 5

Senne Lammens provides a calmness that others can build off but Darlow seemed to do the opposite on his United debut. Was far too indecisive in coming for Jaouen Hadjam’s through ball that Charalampos Kostoulas scored from. Too often seemed to get his positioning wrong but made a crucial stop late on to keep United in the game for a bit longer.

Diogo Dalot – 4

Never quite got to grips with Brighton’s threat down his side and was given a warning when he switched off and didn’t track the run when Malick Yalcouye ran through the lines to be clear on goal, only to shoot wide. His reckless and aimless hooked clearance left United all at sea for Brighton to score their second goal. An experienced player who didn’t use his experience with so much youth surrounding him.

Leny Yoro – 5

Only his second start of season and this wasn’t a ringing endorsement for more. The young Frenchman did make a number of key interceptions in the first half but neither he nor Heaven looks like the vocal leader in the Harry Maguire mould that any good partnership needs. Looked all at sea for Brighton’s third goal. Deserves some credit for the crucial block he made to stop a near-certain goal with 10 minutes to go.

Ayden Heaven – 4

A very difficult night. Was caught in two minds when both he and Darlow hesitated on the stroke of half-time for Brighton to get their first, found himself way too far from Yoro to leave a gaping hole for the second and was not alert to the danger for the third as he missed the key challenge when Noussair Mazraoui had already blown his assignment.

Ayden Heaven endured a difficult night as Brighton came from 2-0 down to win it 3-2

Noussair Mazraoui – 5

Took a nasty whack from Costinha 20 minutes in and required lengthy treatment but carried on. Plays left back for Morocco and was doing OK here before his deficiencies showed and Brighton exposed his lack of pace for the decisive third goal.

Youri Tielemans – 7

Wearing the captain’s armband, Tielemans came out of this as United’s best player, albeit not a high bar to clear. His vision picked out Lacey for the opening goal and he worked hard at the other end when he made a brilliant last-ditch challenge on Kostoulas late in the first half to deny a goal. Showed some pieces of skill that were highlight worthy, but again like Dalot, Carrick needed to see an experienced player do more to stop the bleeding in a game like this.

Andrey Santos – 5

Had played less than 45 minutes since starting away at Hull City having fallen down the pecking order. This was a rare opportunity and while the Brazilian did make some key interceptions, this wasn’t a performance that exactly made a compelling case for regular starts.

Shea Lacey – 6

A magic moment for a special young player. Lacey was making his first career start for United and netted, in typical Lacey fashion for those who watched him in the academy, his first senior goal, a stunner. Produced a brilliant spin move on the touchline to bamboozle Hadjam, who got a booking for dragging him down. Faded slightly but a bright spot on another grim night.

Shea Lacey became the first United teenager in a decade to score on their first start

Mason Mount – 5

Scored the second goal of the game in smart fashion by crashing an effort into the ground and then the roof of the net. But on a night where he had every chance to take control of a game in the No 10 position that is forever locked down by Bruno Fernandes, Mount became a non-factor after the goal. The disappointment on his face when he came off said it all.

Marcus Rashford – 6

Gave Costinha nightmares and his pace is such a valuable weapon to United. But he had the chance to equalise when through one on one. He looked offside but no flag came and it was a wonder save by Steele to deny him. A player of Rashford’s quality has to score that, though. Was a defining moment on the night.

Benjamin Sesko – 4

Did produce some clever touches to bring team-mates into play and was inches away from nicking the ball past an onrushing Steele as Brighton’s back-pass attempt fell short before the hour. But he didn’t manage a single effort on goal in 65 minutes before coming off on a rough night. It doesn’t feel like he or United know how to get the best out of him.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 4

Turn that pressure dial up a notch. He demanded more intensity from his players as this one got away from them and by the end he had his stars out there trying to salvage a cup run. It was all in vain and the noise around his position only gets louder from here.

SUBS

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
