The IGP made the call while delivering a keynote address at the 2026 Men’s Mental Health Conference, organised by the Peace Progress & Unity Global Initiative (PPUGI), with the theme, “Providing Direction and Support 5.0: Breaking the Silence — Mental Health Support for Our Men (Security Personnel).”

Represented by the Force Medical Director, AIG Nkechi Eze, the IGP noted that the mental health needs of security personnel had been neglected for far too long and therefore deserved urgent and sustained attention.

According to him, mentally healthy security personnel were better equipped to serve effectively and contribute to a safer and more secure nation.

He emphasised that mental health was not a sign of weakness, but an essential component of human wellbeing, productivity, responsible leadership, sound decision-making and effective service delivery.

According to a statement by the Force Medical Public Relations/Liaison Officer, Directorate of Force Medical Services, SP Eze Chidiebere, the IGP highlighted the unique psychological demands associated with policing and other security-related duties, noting that officers are routinely exposed to difficult and, at times, traumatic experiences.

“They respond to crime scenes, confront dangerous situations, witness human suffering, interact with victims and distressed families, and make critical decisions under immense pressure,” he said.

The IGP stressed that behind every uniform is a human being with emotions, vulnerabilities and personal challenges that must be acknowledged and appropriately supported.

He called for stronger institutional mechanisms to promote mental health awareness, facilitate early intervention and provide access to professional psychosocial support, as well as foster a culture in which personnel can seek help without fear of stigma or discrimination.

World.title: South Africa weather report: today’s most dangerous warning

The Northern Cape stays partly cloudy, with isolated thundershowers in Kimberley, reaching 22°C. Upington stays partly cloudy with a top of 23°C.

A Yellow Level 2 warning for damaging winds covers the southern parts of the province.

A cold, wet and windy advisory also covers the southern Northern Cape until Friday.



WHY THE EAST AND SOUTH CARRY THE HEAVIEST WARNINGS TODAY

George turns cloudy with scattered showers and rain, reaching just 16°C.

A Yellow Level 2 warning for damaging winds covers the northern parts of the province.



A cold, wet and windy advisory covers the Cape Winelands, Central Karoo and Little Karoo Districts until Friday, with light snowfall possible over the high-lying areas.

The Eastern Cape turns cloudy, with widespread showers and rain in Gqeberha and East London, both topping out between 15°C and 16°C.

A Yellow Level 2 warning for disruptive rain covers the southern and extreme eastern parts of the province, with localised flooding, road disruptions and power outages possible.



A cold, wet and windy advisory also covers the Eastern Cape until Friday.

KwaZulu-Natal carries the heaviest warning in the country today.

Durban and Richards Bay both turn cloudy with widespread showers and rain, with Durban reaching a top of just 18°C.

It’s a genuinely serious warnings day, with KwaZulu-Natal’s Orange Level 6 warning standing out as the most severe alert in the country today.

It’s worth taking real precautions if you’re anywhere along the KwaZulu-Natal coast, given the danger-to-life language in this warning.

World.title: Springbok Women ready to start new challenge
World.content:
There are some changes to the Springbok Women side that created four tries against the Black Ferns in Johannesburg two weekends ago, with the coaching staff having opted for a rejigged backline and one change to the pack.

Logan Welman will start the match at No 8, swopping places with Aseza Hele, who will play off the bench in the only change to the run-on side up front.

Amongst the backs, Felicia Jacobs and Maria Tshiremba will earn starts after missing out on the Soweto showpiece, while Maceala Samboya – who started on the bench against the Black Ferns before replacing injured Zintle Mpupha at outside centre – keeps that jersey to partner Aphiwe Ngwevu in midfield.



Jacobs and Tshiremba return after playing against Fiji last month, where the latter scored a hat-trick on debut.

HOW THE SPRINGBOK WOMEN WILL LINE UP

Springbok Women: 15 Byrhandré Dolf, 14 Maria Tshiremba, Maceala Samboya, 12 Aphiwe Ngwevu, 11 Ayanda Malinga, 10 Libbie Janse van Rensburg, 9 Felicia Jacobs, 8 Logan Welman, 7 Catha Jacobs, 6 Sizophila Solontsi, 5 Danelle Lochner, 4 Vainah Ubisi, 3 Babalwa Latsha, (captain),2 Lindelwa Gwala, 1 Sanelisiwe Charlie,

Replacements: 16 Micke Gunter, 17 Xoliswa Khuzwayo, 18 Nombuyekezo Mdliki, 19 Nomsa Mokwai, 20 Aseza Hele, 21 Sinelitha Noxeke, 22 Jakkie Cilliers, 23 Patience Mokone

Springbok Women co-coach Franzel September said changes were always on the cards as they want to use the WXV tour to build squad depth and provide starting opportunities to those who have played off the bench in their recent Test matches.



“We are well underway towards the 2029 Women’s Rugby World Cup, not only in our planning, but also giving players experience at the highest level, something that this WXV Global Series will provide. This opening weekend is important for us, as we need to set the tone for the remaining two matches. So, we kept to what we know but also recognize that we need to expand our base,” explains September.

He added they expect a massive forwards battle, as that has been a hallmark of both sides in recent years.

“Yes, it will be huge in the set phases, as both of us are strong in that department. I am happy with our progress in that area of our game in the eight matches we have played this year, but we know Wales will ask different questions here in Cardiff. We prepared well and will be ready for the challenge.”



Interesting move on the bench

Utility forward Sinelitha Noxeke has been added for a six-two split and bomb squad feel, while Jakkie Cilliers and Patience Mokone will cover the backline positions. Cilliers will be the back-up scrumhalf for this match, the first since 2021 between the sides.

Babalwa Latsha, who made her debut at Cardiff Arms Park in 2018, will again lead the team with Libbie Janse van Rensburg, who scored a try in the Springbok Women’s last appearance at the same venue in 2021, the vice-captain.

World.title: Does the SASSA algorithm discriminate against beneficiaries?
World.content:
The Supreme Court of Appeal (SCA) has reserved judgment after hearing that the SASSA algorithm might discriminate against certain beneficiaries. Image: AI generated, for illustrative purposes only

The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) algorithm used to verify beneficiary income has had its day in front of the Supreme Court of Appeal (SCA) in Bloemfontein. The matter pertains to SASSA’s automated bank-verification system that sees no difference between income, family contribution or stokvel payouts …

Better understanding of the SASSA algorithm is part of the same appeal we’ve reported on extensively. This originates from the January 2025 Gauteng High Court ruling that found key parts of SASSA SRD regulations were unconstitutional. Last month, Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana told the Supreme Court of Appeal (SCA) that the National Treasury, “simply cannot afford to do more”, for the country’s poor.

SASSA ALGORITHM ON TRIAL

Fascinatingly, the Global Center on Governance (GCG) for AI, represented by the Centre for Applied Legal Studies, joined the argument. It argued to the SCA that the fully automated SASSA algorithm represents not only a funding problem, but a constitutional problem. The GCG explains that the current SASSA system treats any deposit into an applicant’s bank account as financial means.



As such, the SASSA algorithm has no in-built mechanism to distinguish between a salary, loan from a relative, stokvel contribution, or money held on someone else’s behalf, for example. It argues, in a country where large numbers of people rely on informal and shared financial networks rather than formal employment, it is a blunt and ineffective instrument …

RIGHT TO SOCIAL SECURITY

A loan, gift or stokvel payout should not trigger the SASSA algorithm against beneficiaries, argues the GCG. Image: File

Furthermore, the submission argues that all South Africans have constitutional rights to social security, equality and dignity. There are also possibly some knock-on effects for Section 71 of the automated handling of personal identify data through the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA).

Meanwhile, government’s counsel defended the online system on practical grounds. It argued it’s how the agency is able to process around 15- to 18-million applicants a month. This is a volume no human-staffed system could realistically replicate. Likewise, government says it would need an additional R93 billion to account for all 18 million monthly applicants.

WHEN WILL THE SCA RULE?

Accordingly, the SCA has reserved judgment on the state’s appeal after hearing arguments on 25 August 2026. And no specific date has been announced for the final ruling yet. Plus, further appeals are likely if the ruling does not go the state’s way. However, a SASSA algorithm that can’t tell a stokvel payout from a loan, or a salary risks wrongfully excluding the exact people the SASSA grant was built for in the first place.

But what do you think? Do you think the SASSA algorithm discriminates against certain beneficiaries? Do you have any first-hand experience of this yourself? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Lifetime opportunity at Kaizer Chiefs: Renaldo Leaner to replace Brandon Petersen
World.content:
The 28 year old Renaldo Leaner joined the club only a couple of months ago. He is now widely expected to replace captain and first choice goalkeeper Brandon Petersen in the starting lineup.

Petersen has been ruled out for up to six weeks after suffering a medial collateral ligament injury to his left knee during Tuesday morning’s training session.

For Leaner, Sunday’s Betway Premiership clash against Lamontville Golden Arrows at Mbombela Stadium could therefore be the beginning of a career changing spell.



DOES RENALDO LEANER HAVE THE NUMBERS?

Leaner arrives with 62 senior club appearances, 21 clean sheets, three Bafana Bafana caps and a standout record of producing under pressure.

The Elsies River native came through the Ajax Cape Town academy before gaining senior experience with Maritzburg United and Sekhukhune United.

His 2022/23 campaign with Maritzburg United produced six clean sheets in 16 appearances, while his overall senior club record stands at 21 clean sheets and 59 goals conceded in 62 appearances.

One of his most impressive performances came against Orlando Pirates while playing for Sekhukhune United.

Leaner made five decisive saves in that match, with four coming from inside the box. He also recorded 13 recoveries and claimed two high balls as he secured a memorable clean sheet.

His performances have earned him a 7.4 average FotMob rating during his active top flight minutes.



WHAT MAKES LEANER DIFFERENT?

The goalkeeper’s domestic form eventually led to international recognition with Bafana Bafana.

Leaner has three caps for South Africa and kept two clean sheets in his first three international matches. He made his debut against Tanzania and also featured against Panama.

Away from football, Leaner has an impressive academic background. He holds a Bachelor of Education from the University of the Western Cape, a Sports Psychology qualification from UNISA and a Higher Certificate in Sports Sciences from Tuks.

CAN HE HANDLE THE KAIZER CHIEFS PRESSURE?

Replacing Petersen means stepping into one of the most scrutinised positions in South African football.

Kaizer Chiefs have previously relied on legendary goalkeepers including Brian Baloyi, Rowen Fernandez and Itumeleng Khune. Khune in particular set an exceptional standard with his shot stopping and distribution.

Leaner will now have to handle those expectations when he faces Golden Arrows, the same opponents who ended Kaizer Chiefs’ MTN8 campaign earlier this season with Petersen in goal.

COULD THIS BE HIS BIG BREAK?

Leaner will need to command his penalty area, organise the defence and distribute accurately while making the crucial saves at Mbombela Stadium.

A strong run could turn a six week injury replacement role into something far more significant for Leaner at Kaizer Chiefs. He has already played at top flight level, represented Bafana Bafana and delivered against major opposition.

Now, he has the opportunity to prove that he can do it for Kaizer Chiefs.

WHAT DO YOU EXPECT FROM HIM?

Share your thoughts by clicking on the red comments block below.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs news: Petersen ruled out for six weeks
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs captain Brandon Petersen has been ruled out for four to six weeks due to injury, the club confirmed on Wednesday.

The 32-year-old keeper has played in all the club’s games this season.

In recent weeks, Petersen has made costly errors which led to goals. Amakhosi confirmed that their keeper was injured during training on Tuesday.



“Goalkeeper Brandon Petersen sustained a knee injury during training on Tuesday morning and will be sidelined for an estimated four to six weeks. The experienced shot-stopper, who has featured in every match since the season kicked off in August, injured the medial collateral ligament in his left knee and will now undergo rehabilitation,” Chiefs said in a statement.

Chiefs to replace Petersen

With Petersen injured, Chiefs could field Renaldo Leaner or Bruce Bvuma.

Adding to the concerns, attacker Wandile Duba has been ruled out for approximately two weeks after picking up a hip and groin injury.

Duba, who has already netted three goals this season, has a minor defect in the affected area, and the medical team will monitor his progress closely over the coming week before determining the next course of action.

Both players have played key roles in Kaizer Chiefs’ strong start to the campaign, and their absence will be felt.

Who should replace Petersen?

World.title: Sol Phenduka sorry for Kempton Park runner ‘joke’ [video]
World.content:
Sol Phenduka has apologised for his comments about a Kempton Park murder victim. Images via X

Podcast and Chil co-presenter Sol Phenduka has apologised for his comments mocking one of the Kempton Park murder victims – Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo.

The media personality made the comments during a recent episode filmed alongside MacG, whose real name is MacGyver Mukwevho.

To date, the bodies of 8 women have been discovered, some of whom were found partially naked and sexually assaulted. The perpetrator – whom some have labelled a “serial killer” – has not been found.



SOL PHENDUKA SORRY OVER KEMPTON PARK ‘JOKE’

In a video posted on his social media platforms, Sol Phenduka claimed that his comments about a Kempton Park woman who had been kidnapped – now identified as runner Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo – had been recorded over the weekend, before her family identified her body at a Germiston mortuary.

He said, “I made an unfortunate pun or joke. At the time, we laughed. But it’s not funny anymore.

“I want to profusely apologise to South Africans, to chillers and to her family”/

“Deriving a joke, be it targeting someone else, about a situation involving a missing person, is distasteful. It is a traumatic situation. Especially in the context of South Africa and the high femicide that we have”.

Sol Phenduka stated that he was an anti-gender-based violence advocate and “would never make light of such a tragic moment”.

He also pleaded with his male followers to “stop the violence”.



“It’s mostly men who are the perpetrators”, he added.

WHAT DID HE SAY?

In a clip from Podcast and Chill released on Monday, Sol Phenduka and MacG casually spoke about a woman who had gone missing in Kempton Park.

At the time of recording, the woman – now identified as Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo – had not been confirmed dead.

Sol joked that an opportunistic individual had abducted the woman, hoping to cash in on a big payday in ransom money.

I honestly don’t find this funny. I’m utterly disgusted. I’m especially disappointed in Sol. As for MacG , I’m not shocked that he would make fun of the Kempton Park situation on his huge podcast. His platform was built on belittling and bullying Black women. pic.twitter.com/q1yAmAZd02 — La-Ndlovu (@destiny_ndlovu) September 16, 2026

Over the years, Podcast and Chill’s Sol Phenduka and MacG have come under fire for making derogatory comments about women.

The list includes high-profile women like activist and actress Rosie Motene, media personality Amanda du Pont, singer Kelly Khumalo, and, most recently, Minnie Dlamini.

World.title: ‘I call for his inclusion at Bafana’: Pirates legend disappointed by Brandon Petersen
World.content:
Orlando Pirates legend Benedict Tso Vilakazi has lashed on Kaizer Chiefs goalkeeper Brandon Petersen.

The Amakhosi captain has made four msitakes this season which had led to goals.

Vilakazi, who called for the Kaizer Chiefs keeper to be included in the Bafana squad, has expressed his disappoitment at the 32-year-old star.



I’m disappointed,” said Tso on iDiski TV.

“Why am I disappointed is that when we call your name to go represent us at the national team, and then you come and then make a mistake like this, then I don’t know. I’m not saying he’s not a keeper that should not concede goals, but not like this. Like this, no, it’s uncalled for.

“I’m trying to put nice words in the action itself because it’s an easy thing. Step up, stand in that pole, the ball hits you here [on the body], you get the ball, done, finished. But Petersen I don’t know what he was thinking, and again, it shows me that he didn’t have that eye contact with the ball from that distance of that corner flag swinging in coming here.”

Petersen disappoints Tso

“I mean really, he should see that. I mean your action, you are covering. I know maybe somebody will argue and say the ball had power. I get it. But you are saying that seeing that ball from that corner flag… It’s possible,” Vilakazi added.

Petersen will not play Chiefs next game due to injury.

Who should be in goals for Amakhosi in the next match?

World.title: Desperate search under way for missing hiker on Table Mountain
World.content:
Wayne Barnard was last seen wearing a khaki green puffer jacket, bottle-green cargo pants and black sneakers. Image: Supplied

A desperate search is under way for a 46-year-old man who reportedly went missing while hiking alone on Table Mountain.

A missing-persons poster circulating on local hiking and trail-running WhatsApp groups identifies the man as Wayne Barnard.

According to the poster, Barnard last made contact at 11:05 on Wednesday, 16 September. He had shared his location and a photograph from Table Mountain.



His phone has since been switched off or is unreachable.

Barnard was hiking alone at the time. A South African Police Service (SAPS) missing-persons case has reportedly been opened.

The trail-running group RunTnT shared the poster, accompanied by the following message: “Missing hiker on Table Mountain. Search under way – Wilderness Search and Rescue (WSAR) & SAPS. Please keep a lookout if you happen to be in the area, or are still on the mountain. Please share the post as needed.”



Missing hiker last seen in khaki jacket

Barnard is described as a white male with brown/grey hair. He is approximately 1.91 metres tall and weighs around 90kg.

At the time of his disappearance, he was reportedly wearing a khaki green O’Neill puffer jacket, bottle-green cargo pants and black sneakers.

The poster urges members of the public to share the information widely, particularly with hikers, trail runners, climbers and the wider Cape Town community.



The appeal comes amid growing concern over the safety of hikers and trail runners who regularly use Table Mountain National Park’s extensive network of trails.



Community asked to share information

The missing-person notice provides contact details for Barnard’s family and for SANParks Emergency Services.

Anyone with information about Wayne Barnard’s whereabouts is urged to contact Lauren Barnard on +27 82 755 0246.



SANParks Emergency Services can also be contacted on +27 71 807 8374.

Barnard’s mobile number is listed on the poster too: +27 78 775 5816.

World.title: Masemola's legal team raises concerns over IDAC investigation
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The legal team representing suspended National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola says the Independent Directorate for Anti-Corruption (IDAC) was overly ambitious in pursuing charges against the top cop.

The comments come after the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) withdrew charges against Masemola in the Medicare24 SAPS tender case.

However, the matter must still return to court, where the withdrawal of the charges is expected to be formally recorded.

Masemola’s lawyer, Morongoe Seleka, says the defence reached its conclusions after reviewing the police docket and thousands of pages of evidence.

“We have seen from the disclosure of the police docket, the records that have been supplied to us in consideration of what exactly General Masemola is being charged with,” Seleka said.

He said the defence team had been required to examine more than 30,000 pages of material.

Seleka argued that their review of the docket raised serious questions about the investigation and the charges brought against Masemola.

“We have come to the conclusion that this is a serious misplacement of the investigative mandate of IDAC and also prosecutorial duties that IDAC has, in terms of the legislation, been mandated with,” he said.

Seleka went further, describing IDAC’s decision to pursue the charges as “judicial overreach”.

World.title: Mapisa-Nqakula to continue testimony in corruption trial
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula is back in the North Gauteng High Court, where she is expected to continue testifying in her defence in her corruption trial.

The State is expected to question Mapisa-Nqakula on each of the 12 corruption charges she faces, as well as one count of money laundering.

Her return to the witness stand follows the court’s dismissal of her application to have the charges against her struck off.

Mapisa-Nqakula had previously taken a break from the trial due to ill health.

She has denied allegations that she solicited or received payments from defence contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu.

The State alleges that payments were made to Mapisa-Nqakula during her time as Speaker of the National Assembly. She has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

World.title: Enough is enough: Kempton Park residents march over killings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Residents in Kempton Park and surrounding communities are taking to the streets on Thursday, demanding urgent action following the deaths of women in the area.

The march follows the discovery of the bodies of eight women over a two-month period, raising growing concerns about the safety of women and children in the community.

Residents say they are deeply concerned about the threat facing women and children and are calling on authorities to do more to protect them.

Protesters are marching from the Kempton Park Civic Centre to the local police station, where they are expected to call for stronger action, increased police visibility and greater accountability from law enforcement authorities.

World.title: Messi heads Inter Miami to Campeones Cup triumph
World.content:
MIAMI - Lionel Messi headed a goal and provided an assist as Inter Miami won the Campeones Cup on Wednesday, beating Cruz Azul 2-0 in the annual clash between Major League Soccer and Mexican Liga MX champions.

It was Inter Miami's first Campeones Cup triumph and came thanks to the Argentine superstar's 100th goal for the reigning MLS Cup winners. A late Messi corner was headed home by Casemiro to seal the win.

Victory gave Messi his first trophy of the year, two months after the heartbreak of losing the 2026 World Cup final to Spain with Argentina.

The trophy came in new head coach Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez's first game in charge of Miami.

Argentine manager Gonzalez was appointed last month, but due to visa delays only took his first training sessions this week.

Cruz Azul had the game's first big chance, Jose Paradela's shot saved at the near post by Miami goalkeeper Dayne St Clair.

Miami's opener came in the 24th minute. Though the goalscorer was no surprise, it was a rare Messi header that broke the deadlock.

Luis Suarez crossed from the byline, and the 5-foot-7 Messi outjumped Willer Ditta with a diving header to give Miami the lead.

Suarez nearly turned provider again in the 32nd minute. He received a sumptuous cross-field ball from Messi and scooped it up for German Berterame, whose dinked effort was cleared off the line.

Early in the second half Messi appeared to have scored his 101st Miami goal, racing through one-on-one from a Suarez through ball and placing his shot in off the post, but was ruled offside.

Cruz Azul should have equalised in the 67th minute, but substitute Gabriel Fernandez's glancing header hit the post, and Casemiro blocked the follow-up shot.

A Messi corner gave Miami the two-goal cushion, finding Casemiro, who nodded the ball low to the far post in the 81st minute.

St Clair denied Cruz Azul a late consolation, saving well from a Paradela free kick.

The annual Campeones Cup pits the previous year's MLS Cup winner against the winner of Mexico's Campeon de Campeones.

It was the eighth edition of the cup, which is always hosted by the MLS participant.

Mexican teams had won the three most recent editions before Miami's victory on Wednesday.

Mexican giants Cruz Azul have still never won the Campeones Cup. They lost the 2021 final.

World.title: US stocks fall, dollar gains after Fed lifts interest rates
World.content:
NEW YORK - Wall Street stocks fell while the dollar advanced Wednesday after the Federal Reserve lifted interest rates for the first time since 2023.

A rate increase had been widely anticipated, but markets judged the central bank's overall message as more hawkish than expected after a majority of Fed policymakers penciled in at least one more rate hike before the end of 2026.

All three major US stock indices finished lower, with the broad-based S&P 500 down 0.5 percent.

The dollar advanced against the euro and other major currencies, while increases in Treasury yields indicated that the market believes from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's commentary that "the inflation fight isn't a one-and-done rate-hike kind of thing," said Briefing.com.

"The remarks have reinforced the view that today's rate hike may not be an isolated move, with investors focused on the possibility that persistent inflation pressures could require additional tightening in the months ahead."

The US central bank's Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously to raise rates to between 3.75 and 4.00 percent, citing "elevated" inflation and adding that the rate hike would support a "timelier return" to its two-percent target for the metric.

Warsh, who was appointed by US President Donald Trump, said the decision was a "serious" one, but needed to be taken.

"The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has been for too long," he told a press conference.

But Warsh's move may spark blowback from Trump, who relentlessly criticised former Fed chair Jerome Powell over rate decisions. Trump has also launched an unprecedented assault on the Fed's independence since taking office, attempting to fire a Fed governor and promoting a criminal probe against Powell.

Following the Fed's announcement, White House spokesperson Kush Desai said the decision was "rather unfortunate" and that Trump had been clear that he wanted lower interest rates.

Earlier, bourses in Europe had gotten a lift as oil prices dropped after a US industry report pointed to a pickup in stockpiles.

Analysts also pointed to talk that an outage of a key pipeline for Saudi oil may be resolved in a matter of days.

The Fed's decision will be followed on Thursday by the Bank of England, which is expected to leave its benchmark rate unchanged as weak UK economic growth offsets high inflation.

Official data Wednesday showed UK annual inflation remained above the BoE's two-percent target, reaching 3.1 percent in August on surging fuel prices.

The Bank of Japan is expected to hike rates on Friday owing to rising inflation and the need to maintain support for the yen.

Investors are also watching a planned summit between Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, with reports that they could agree to some tariff reductions.

World.title: 'Breathing toxin every day': Indonesians choked by haze feel helpless
World.content:
JAKARTA - Struggling to breathe through the acrid haze emanating from wildfires on Indonesia's Borneo island, residents told AFP on Wednesday they feared for their health but had little to do but wait out the foul-smelling hazard.

Indonesia, which shares Borneo with Malaysia and Brunei, is grappling with forest fires that have ravaged swathes of the island, partly caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon that has also affected other countries in Southeast Asia and beyond.

In Pontianak, the capital of West Kalimantan province, the thick, yellow smoke was so intense that it had paralysed the international airport over the weekend.

"My eyes sting, my head hurts. Over the past week it's been getting worse," resident Anggita Putri told AFP.

"While working, my chest feels tight, my head dizzy, my eyes burning. Even with this unhealthy air, we still must work," she said.

The air quality index for Pontianak briefly exceeded 1,100 over the weekend, Anggita said -- nearly four times the hazardous limit.

"I leave my child at home, so of course I have worries that go beyond just my own health. I'm also concerned about my child's condition," said the 28-year-old, who has a three-year-old son.

Another Pontianak resident, 35-year-old university lecturer Djunita Permata Indah, also said she was concerned for her two children, aged two and four.

"The situation is quite bad. I'm worried about the children's health. Even as an adult, I feel my head aching and dizzy because of the smoky air," she told AFP.

"But parents still must work, so the children are forced to keep going to daycare, where they remain exposed to the smoke that has already started to enter the house."

The health ministry said last week that more than 113,000 cases of upper respiratory tract infections had been recorded across seven provinces since the fires began to rage early this year.

Brief rainfall on Tuesday, which some residents had hoped could alleviate the risk, did little to help and only intensified the thick smoke, Djunita said.

Local authorities said they were intensifying efforts to bring the haze under control, including by water bombing and cloud seeding.

- 'Surrounded by smoke' -

Indonesia regularly battles wildfires during the dry season, which typically runs from July to October, but the blazes this year have been particularly bad in part because the powerful El Nino -- expected to be the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago.

Experts also blame climate change, decades of forest degradation and slash-and-burn land clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape.

From Borneo, the haze has also spread to neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia.

The Indonesian government has said that between January and July, more than 202,000 hectares of land burned across the country.

The Nusantara Atlas project put that figure close to 300,000 for the same period, and last week estimated the total area affected, including August, was nearly 896,000 hectares.

President Prabowo Subianto has vowed to go after corporations found to be responsible for fires.

"If it is clearly established that they are responsible, we must revoke all of their permits," he said in Jakarta on Wednesday.

"And if necessary, even after their permits are revoked, we will continue to investigate any criminal elements. There will be no mercy from now on."

For many residents on Borneo, the haze has not only affected their health but also disrupted their livelihood.

"My house is surrounded by smoke... For more than a month, I haven't opened the windows," said snack seller Desia, who like many Indonesians only has one name.

She told AFP she had stopped working two weeks ago because she could no longer spend much time outside.

"It's like we're breathing toxin every day," she said.

Desia's two children, aged 10 and 11, have not gone to school in over a month, spending most of their time in the only room in the house that has an air purifier.

"Right now, I just hope for rain," she said. "I've stopped hoping for anything from the government."

World.title: Watts, Pitt, Cruz to light up Spain's top film festival
World.content:
MADRID - Hollywood stars Naomi Watts, Brad Pitt and Penelope Cruz are due to grace Spain's San Sebastian Film Festival from Friday, where great expectations await a mini-series by Chile's Pablo Larrain.

Marion Cotillard, Orlando Bloom, Ricardo Darin, Jeremy Irons, Rami Malek and Diego Luna are among the other big names expected on the red carpet between September 18-26 in the northern coastal city.

Watts, 57, will receive the "Donostia" lifetime achievement award on Saturday after organisers hailed her as "one of the most talented and recognised actresses of her generation".

The British-born Australian earned two Oscar nominations for her roles in "21 Grams" (2003) by Mexican director Alejandro Gonzalez Inarritu and "The Impossible" (2012) under Spain's Juan Antonio Bayona.

The opening day of the festival's 74th edition will see veteran German director Werner Herzog pick up the other "Donostia" award in recognition of a career with around 70 films to his name.

A total of 17 movies are vying in the official section for the top awards before a jury presided by US director Ira Sachs.

In the running for the Golden Shell prize for best film is Larrain's "My Sad Dead", a mini-series based on the stories of Argentine writer Mariana Enriquez.

Known for his films "No", "Neruda" and a trilogy that explored the lives of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, Princess Diana and Maria Callas, Larrain tells the story of a recently retired doctor who can see the dead.

Jesse Eisenberg, best known for acting performances in movies such as "The Social Network", features in his third long-format production "The Debut".

Out of competition, Brad Pitt represents "Heart of the Beast" by David Ayer, in which he plays a military official who suffers an air accident and is trapped with his dog in Alaska.

World.title: Santaco pledges support for women in fight against GBV
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African taxi industry has pledged its commitment to supporting women in the fight against gender-based violence (GBV).

The South African National Taxi Council (Santaco) said it is actively engaging with drivers, marshals and other industry workers to help them understand GBV and femicide, as well as how to respond when they witness such incidents.

According to Santaco spokesperson Rebecca Phala, these conversations are translating into real-life action.

“We understand that we’ve got that responsibility. If it’s super early in the morning, we need to just go an extra mile to meet the commuter where they are. Obviously, we’ve been keeping with the right rules of the road.

“That’s just one of the many things we do to make sure that people feel safe and that they are encouraged to continue using our vehicles,” she said.

Phala said Santaco had recorded numerous incidents in which women ran into taxi ranks while being chased or feeling threatened, as they believed they would be protected there.

However, she acknowledged that more training is needed on how to handle such cases when they are brought to the industry’s attention, particularly for drivers and marshals.

“They interact with a lot of people on a daily basis, so it's about offering that layer of support.”

World.title: Why Uhuru is sending shivers down Ruto's spine
World.content:
Former President Uhuru Kenyatta and President William Ruto. [File, Standard]

Outrage greeted President William Ruto's latest assault on the character of former President Uhuru Kenyatta when he labelled him a "rebel leader", a tag they say pained his predecessor, a lawless leader associated with either rag-tag armies or armed militia groups.

Uhuru might have left office more than four years ago, but he is not leaving President William Ruto’s lips anytime soon, as his predecessor anchors his reelection campaign on bashing Uhuru at every opportunity.

World.title: Five killed as bandits ambush police search team in Isiolo
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Five people, including two police officers killed by bandits at the troubled grazing field of Gotu in Isiolo County on Wednesday.

The victims are a senior police officer, a police constable who was the driver of the vehicle that was ambushed by bandits, a livestock farmer and two National Police Reservists (NPR). The police officers were attached to an Anti-Stock Theft Unit (ASTU) located near Gotu trading centre.

The victims were part of a search team that was looking for an elderly man who reportedly went missing within the Gotu area and was last seen around Madho Gurba Huka, a grazing area in Chari Ward in Merti sub-county.

Isiolo County Police Commander Isaac Sang said the mentally challenged man from Barambate sub-location, Kulamawe location was reported missing a day ago.

The Isiolo camel keeper, reported to be related to the man who went missing, had requested police to search for him.

The mission turned tragic when the group was ambushed by armed bandits, killing all five on the spot.

The incident took place near the junction of Lososia-Merti road and Gotu-Merti route.

Mr Sang said the bodies of the officers and other victims were removed to Isiolo County Teaching and Referral Hospital awaiting postmortem.

"A reinforcement (of security personnel) had been sent to the area which includes an armoured vehicle to pursue the attackers," said the police chief.

The police boss called for calm and cooperation from the residents while police pursue the suspects.

He said that investigation into the incident had commenced.

On Wednesday afternoon, a gunfight was reported between police reservists and the bandits on the western bank of the river.

"The reservists in the area pursued the attackers minutes after reports of the killings that led to an exchange of gunfire. We are told an unknown number of people have been injured," said a herdsman from Gotu who sought anonymity for security reasons.

A source from Isiolo County and Teaching and Referral Hospital revealed that two ambulances had been sent to Gotu to attend to the injured persons.

Gotu, along with Kom in Merti sub-county is a bandit hotspot in Isiolo that is attributed to competition over scarce pasture by rival herders from Isiolo, Samburu East and parts of Marsabit with local leaders calling for eviction of pastoralists from outside the County. Several people have been killed in the two locations since last year and hundreds of livestock stolen.

On August 1, two people were killed in the Garse Dabata area in Gotu and nearly 700 goats and sheep were stolen. Nearly all the stolen animals were recovered in operation undertaken by a multi-agency security team stationed in various locations along the Isiolo-Meru border.

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen on two occasions called for an operation in parts of Isiolo, Laikipia, Samburu and Meru Counties that had experienced frequent cases of banditry and rustling.

However, leaders fault the CS for failure to take decisive action on insecurity that keeps on recurring in parts of Isiolo and Meru Counties. The leaders including Governor Abdi Guyo want herders from outside Isiolo who are in Kom and Gotu areas to be evicted.

World.title: Muthaiga Golf Club restores access after KFS standoff
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Muthaiga Golf Club has restored access to a section of its course that was temporarily taken over by the Kenya Forest Service (KFS), hours after the agency moved into the area, claiming it forms part of Karura Forest.

The disruption affected the Front Nine, covering Holes Two to Nine, before the club’s board intervened to restore normal operations.

In a statement issued Tuesday, Muthaiga Golf Club Chairman Dennis Mwirigi said the board had taken the necessary steps to facilitate the resumption of activities after the temporary disruption.

“We are pleased to confirm that access to the affected part of the course has been restored and members may proceed with their scheduled activities as usual,” Mwirigi said.

He said the board remained committed to protecting the club’s interests, assets and members while addressing the matter through the appropriate channels.

The development follows an earlier communication to members informing them that KFS had taken over access to the affected section, claiming it was part of Karura Forest.

The club had initially said the Front Nine would not be accessible until further notice as it sought to resolve the matter. The driving range and parking areas were not affected.

The incident sparked criticism over the manner in which KFS handled the dispute, with Prof Karanja, Chairperson of Friends of Karura Forest, urging the agency to pursue dialogue and legal channels.

Prof Karanja said KFS should have first engaged the club’s management and clearly explained its claim over the disputed land instead of deploying dogs, guns and heavy security.

“If they don't agree that it was your land, go to court. The court will determine,” he said.

He questioned whether KFS had adequately demonstrated that the disputed section was forest land or explained how it was allegedly acquired by Muthaiga Golf Club.

“They should have come publicly and said, look, Muthaiga, that area and that area belong to the forest,” Prof Karanja said.

He said KFS should identify the specific portion of land it claims belongs to the forest and explain the basis of its claim before taking further action.

Prof Karanja argued that the dispute should be resolved through established legal procedures rather than force. “Trees are not protected by guns,” he said.

He described the deployment of armed personnel as the wrong way of resolving a land dispute and called for engagement between KFS and the golf club.

Prof Karanja also warned that actions by government agencies could have wider implications for the administration of President William Ruto, saying confrontational conduct could lead members of the public to associate such actions directly with the government.

“When government departments behave like this, everybody now starts thinking, oh, it's Ruto's whatever,” he said.

He further recalled a previous dispute involving Friends of Karura Forest, where he said armed personnel were deployed and the group removed from an area before senior government officials intervened.

According to Prof Karanja, officials from the Treasury and forestry departments eventually intervened and encouraged dialogue to resolve the matter.

He urged KFS to adopt a similar approach in the Muthaiga dispute, saying the agency and the club should present their respective claims and seek a court determination if they cannot agree.

For now, the restoration of access means members can resume their scheduled activities, while the underlying dispute over the contested section remains subject to further engagement between KFS and the club.

World.title: Juja couple's surprise blessing of five babies
World.content:
Mercy Kanini, 28, from Juja, Kiambu County, gave birth to five children at Thika Level Five Hospital. [Gitau Wanyoike, Standard]

A couple from Juja, Kiambu County, is celebrating the unexpected arrival of five babies after scans during pregnancy showed they were expecting quadruplets.

Mercy Kanini, 28, delivered four girls and a boy through normal delivery at Thika Level Five Hospital, in a rare case believed to be among only a handful of quintuplet births recorded in Kenya.
