NEW DELHI: Two terrorists were neutralised during an overnight counter-terrorism operation in Jammu and Kashmirâs Udhampur district, the Army said on Thursday.The operation, code-named Operation Sohan, was launched during the intervening night of September 16 and 17 following confirmed intelligence inputs about the presence of terrorists in the general area of Brattal, the Armyâs White Knight Corps said.Despite hostile weather, difficult terrain and poor visibility, troops of the White Knight Corps, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) launched a targeted operation in the area, the Army said.Official said that a joint search operation was launched in the remote Bratel Soan and Khubban areas of Majalta around 9 pm on Wednesday following information about the movement of suspected terrorists.A few rounds of firing and blasts, reportedly carried out by security forces while targeting a suspected hideout, were heard in the forest shortly after the operation began, officials said.The area remained largely quiet through the night before the lull ended on Thursday morning, when the terrorists opened heavy fire in an attempt to break the security forcesâ cordon.Security forces retaliated, triggering an encounter that continued in the forested area.The Army later said the operation resulted in the neutralisation of two terrorists. Search and surveillance operations are continuing in the area, while security forces remain deployed to track and neutralise any remaining threat, the White Knight Corps said.The operation comes amid heightened security activity in the Pir Panjal region following the recent busting of an alleged overground worker (OGW) network linked to the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) in Rajouri.On September 15, Rajouri Police arrested three people in connection with an alleged terror module operating in the Pir Panjal region. According to police, the three were allegedly involved in providing logistical support, safe transit and other ground-level assistance to terrorists operating in the region.Preliminary investigation found that the accused allegedly worked as guides and helped facilitate the movement of terrorist groups towards the Kashmir Valley, police said. They were also suspected of providing ground support to terrorists linked to multiple high-profile attacks, including an attack targeting civilians.Police also recovered an improvised explosive device (IED) based on information provided by one of the accused.According to officials, preliminary findings indicated that the IED had allegedly been handed over to the accused by members of a terrorist group for safe custody and possible use in a targeted attack.The recovery of the IED and the arrests have provided investigators with leads into the wider terror network operating in the region, police said.

World.title: Maratha activist Jarange Patil calls off 20-day fast, gives govt 3 months to consider demands
World.content:
Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike.

NEW DELHI: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange Patil on Thursday called off his 20-day-old hunger strike and gave the Maharashtra government three months to consider his demands, news agency PTI reported.The decision came after Jarange addressed a large gathering at Patoda in Beed district around 2 am, raising concerns about his worsening physical condition and the possibility of abandoning his planned march to Mumbai.Jarange, who had entered the day 18 of his fast at the time of the address, said he was too physically exhausted to continue a long journey with thousands of supporters travelling behind him.He asked Maratha community members not to follow his vehicle after he left Patoda. Instead, he urged them to meet him directly at Khopoli. He warned that if the convoy continued, he might stop the journey and resume his sit-in protest in Patoda or return to Antarwali Sarati.Despite reaching the venue at around 1.30 am, Jarange found thousands of people, including women, waiting to hear him speak.Addressing the gathering, he said he could barely move his limbs after stopping IV fluids on September 12."Fighting for the children of my community has taken a toll on my body, but I have taken on the government for you. The government wants me to surrender, but should I abandon our demand? My community is greater than any government - it is my father. My community holds the power to bring down any government and install a new one," he asserted.Jarange said the movement had made progress after 58 lakh archival records, known as nondi, were uncovered. He claimed these records could help nearly 2.5 crore members of the Maratha community access reservation benefits.He said the immediate demand was for the Maharashtra government to issue an official gazette recognising the relevant records.The activist also criticised chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, claiming he had countered the government's political moves and that all the documented records had been secured on pen drives. He further accused Fadnavis of "plotting against his life".Responding to the government's argument about fruit orchard owners in Western Maharashtra, Jarange questioned why OBC communities that also own orchards should not receive reservation benefits."The government claims Western Maharashtra has fruit orchards, but don't OBC communities own orchards too? Why do they have a reservation then?"Jarange said it was not possible to continue a rally tour while observing an indefinite hunger strike. He appealed to supporters to avoid following his vehicle and said he would prefer to travel directly to Mumbai from Patoda after speaking to the police, if his health allowed.He also spoke about his family, saying he had asked them to live with self-respect and told his son to remain courageous if he died for the community."I have told my family to live with self-respect. I told my son to step up courageously if I give my life for the community. Let one life be sacrificed for the cause, but never let the dignity of our caste be lowered," he said.

World.title: Good El Nino? How a bad monsoon left Delhi drenched
World.content:
Delhi had a seasonâs rainfall surplus of 8% in a meteorological subdivision (Haryana)

Wet capital

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The capital defied the odds this monsoon. As of Sept 16, Delhi had a season's rainfall surplus of 8% in a meteorological subdivision (Haryana) that's reeling under a 23% deficit and a region (northwest India) that has logged a 10% shortfall. The season's peculiar rainfall pattern indicates that a strengthening El Nino as well as climate change may have played a role in giving the capital an unlikely monsoon bounty.A look at the season's district-level rainfall map of the region shows Delhi literally at the edge of the good monsoon zone this year (see graphic). Just north of the capital lies a swathe of deficient districts starting with neighbouring Sonipat (-32%) and Rohtak (-47%) and all the way up to Hoshiarpur (-53%) and Kapurthala (-69%) in Punjab - a cluster of over 30 rain-starved districts in Haryana and Punjab as well as adjoining Rajasthan, Himachal and west UP.So how did Delhi turn into a wet pocket next to a rain-deficient region? The answer lies in the way low-pressure systems coming from Bay of Bengal shifted direction this season, probably under the influence of El Nino, and how their interactions with westerly disturbances uniquely aided rains in Delhi-NCR.A majority of monsoon rainfall in northwest and central India happens under the influence of moisture-laden low-pressure systems (LPSs), including depressions, travelling inland from Bay of Bengal.Contrary to what one would expect, the number of such systems does not decrease in an El Nino year. In fact, a 2024 study in Climate Dynamics showed that the number of Bay of Bengal depressions increased in El Nino years in the 1979-2020 period, averaging 3.9 during July-Aug versus 2.4 in normal years.This year there were 10 LPSs, including four depressions in July-Aug, against a normal of less than nine.What generally changes in an El Nino year is the direction of the LPSs. "In El Nino years, there is subsidence of air over south India and its adjoining northern parts. This prevents formation of LPSs in the southern latitudes, say in central Bay of Bengal, which would normally move towards the north Andhra-south Odisha coast," said IMD director general Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.Here's where Delhi benefited, particularly in Aug, when as many as six LPSs, including two depressions, impacted India. With a northward shift, most of these systems entered inland over north Odisha-Bengal and tracked north-northwest, affecting Odisha, Bengal, Jharkhand, UP, Uttarakhand and the Delhi region, with lesser impact in Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab.There was another factor in play, likely linked to climate change. WDs are moist wind systems moving east from the Mediterranean region that usually bring wet weather to north India in winter through early summer. Historically, WDs are rare during the monsoons as the jet stream, which causes the disturbance, typically migrates north of the Himalayas by April-May. However, in recent years, the jet stream has persistently been retreating late, a trend scientists attribute to global warming. This year, there were 16 WDs in the June-Aug period - eight in Aug alone, as per IMD.There were several instances of the easterly monsoon system interacting with a WD, intensifying rainfall over parts of north India, including Delhi. For instance, monsoon's onset over the capital on July 2 happened during an active WD spell. The heaviest rain spells in Delhi (July 8-9, July 29, Aug 7-8, Aug 25) occurred when both a monsoon system and a WD were simultaneously active in the region. These interactions also brought heavy rains in west UP and left a catastrophic footprint in the hills - the Bandipora (J&K) cloudburst, fatal flash floods in Chamba (HP) and forced closure of around 290 roads across HP and Uttarakhand - but don't appear to have majorly impacted Haryana and Punjab.

World.title: CGHS 'family' expands, but contribution stays unchanged
World.content:
On Sept 7, the health ministry extended coverage of Central Govt Health Scheme (CGHS) to adopted sisters of scheme beneficiaries. On Sept 1, the eligibility criteria for CGHS was expanded to include married sons and brothers of scheme card holders who are critically or terminally ill.

Over the years, the criteria for beneficiaries have been steadily expanded. Yet the contribution by the cardholder remains the same, unlike in health insurance where the addition of a beneficiary, especially an elderly or ill beneficiary, could entail a steep increase in the premium paid.

According to the Sept 7 office memorandum, the ministry received references "regarding the eligibility of adopted sisters (i.e.

sisters adopted by parents of a CGHS beneficiary) for inclusion as dependent family members under CGHS". The 'sisters' have to be legally adopted by the parents of CGHS beneficiary and have to satisfy the existing criteria of dependency (staying in the same house as the cardholder), income ceiling (not be earning more than Rs 9,000 per month plus the applicable dearness allowance) and marital status (i.e.

be unmarried, divorced, abandoned or separated), as applicable to biological sisters.





The coverage of sons and brothers of beneficiaries was earlier available only to unmarried dependents. There were also age limits of 25 for sons and 18 for brothers, except for those permanently disabled, who were covered for life. The office memorandum issued by the health ministry on Sept 1 spelt out that "marriage shall not constitute a ground for cessation of CHS/medical attendance facilities in respect of dependent son or brother covered under these provisions whether on account of critical/terminal illness or permanent disability.

.."

Also, the lifetime coverage would now also apply for "chronic, severe, critical or terminal illnesses resulting in substantial and continuing functional impairment or inability to earn a livelihood/self-sufficiency".

The addition of critically terminally ill beneficiaries could have a major financial implication for the exchequer as there is no ceiling on the amount spent on CGHS beneficiaries. Since no health insurance would normally cover a critically or terminally ill person, this expansion is fortuitous for an ill person, but only if s/he has a parent or sibling who is a CGHS cardholder.

For dependent daughters and sisters there has never been any age limit but the coverage stops once they get married or get a job with salary above the stipulated limit. Similarly, unmarried/divorced/abandoned/separated daughters and sisters have been eligible for coverage for life, provided they fulfilled the condition of dependency and income. Children and siblings are required to "normally reside" with the primary cardholder to qualify for benefits.

World.title: Bombay Court allows correction of school records even after leaving
World.content:
The Bench of the Bombay High Court at Aurangabad ruled on Wednesday that a student can correct an error in the records of a school or a leaving certificate after leaving the school. The court stated that the reason for leaving the school cannot deny the right to correction. The process requires relevant documents and evidence.

Janabai Himmatrao Thakur applied to the education department to correct her date of birth on a leaving certificate, but her application was rejected because the department claimed she had left school. She then challenged the decision in court.

The government cited Rules 26.3 and 26.4 of the School Code. It stated that correction is allowed during education but not after leaving school. Judgments from the Aurangabad and Nagpur benches differed on this issue. The matter was referred to the Bench.

The Bench clarified the role of relief. It stated that if an error occurred due to oversight or carelessness, the reason for leaving school cannot be used to reject the correction. Correction requires action; the student must provide documents and evidence. The process must follow established rules.

The judgment benefits students with errors in their records or leaving certificates. These errors may include inaccuracies in names, birth dates, or other entries. Such errors can create issues in education, job verification, government schemes, and various processes. The judgment provides relief and paves the way for corrections.

World.title: I’m facing health issues due to hunger strike, tour might be cancelled: Jarange
World.content:
Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange, who is on his way to Mumbai, said on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) that his tour might be cancelled due to health issues arising from long hours of travel and his ongoing hunger strike.

Mr. Jarange reached Patoda in Maharashtra’s Beed district around 11 a.m., nearly 14 hours after setting out from Antarwali Sarati in Jalna, where he launched his fresh round of agitation. He later addressed a gathering there.

The activist said he was facing a severe burning sensation in the stomach and feet.

“If I take treatment, the government becomes completely carefree. If I stop treatment, they become tense. This tour to Mumbai is taking a toll on my health. I can continue if I’m fine, but such long travel is not good amid a hunger strike. The tour can also be cancelled if there is no option,” he said.

Mumbai police earlier denied permission to Mr. Jarange, who has been on a hunger strike for the last 18 days demanding OBC quota for Maratha community members with Kunbi caste genealogies, to take the protest to Azad Maidan, citing law and order concerns during the ongoing Ganesh festival.

Undeterred by the denial, Mr. Jarange on Tuesday (September 15) set out for the Maharashtra capital in a convoy of cars, drawing hundreds of villagers en route who extended their support.

“Reservation is more important than the tour, which seems impossible because of the burning sensation in my stomach and feet,” he told the crowd in Patoda on Wednesday.

Mr. Jarange also appealed to his supporters to let him go to Mumbai alone.

“No vehicle should follow me from Patoda. I will change my route and go to Mumbai. I will only keep the police informed. Please let me go alone. If I am not allowed to enter Mumbai, then you all can come,” he said.

Hinting that the government won't tolerate any intimidating tactics, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis had said on Tuesday that maintaining law and order was the responsibility of the police. He also questioned the timing of the agitation during the Ganesh festival.

The CM said the government had accepted 12 of the 13 "legally valid" demands raised by Maratha protesters.

As per his current plan, Mr. Jarange's carcade will pass through Beed, Srigonda in Ahilyanagar, Hadapsar in Pune and Khopoli in Raigad district before reaching Azad Maidan in Mumbai on September 19, covering more than 400 km.

Mr. Jarange led a major five-day protest and a hunger strike at Azad Maidan on August 29, 2025, demanding Kunbi (OBC) caste certificates for eligible Marathas. The stir was called off on September 2, 2025, after the State government accepted six of eight demands and initiated administrative steps for Kunbi classification certificates.

World.title: Namma Metro: Pink Line may miss September deadline as approvals pending
World.content:
Bengaluru metro’s much-awaited elevated 7.5-km section of the Pink Line may miss yet another deadline to open for passenger services in September, with key regulatory approvals still pending.

The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. (BMRCL) is yet to receive the rolling stock sanction for its application submitted to the Railway Board on September 7. The approval is one of the mandatory steps that needs to be completed before the corridor can be inspected and cleared for commercial operations, according to sources.

Although the State government remains hopeful of launching the corridor this month, operations can begin only after the completion of statutory procedures, including rolling stock approval from the Railway Board and final safety clearance from the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (CMRS).

According to sources, after receiving the rolling stock sanction, BMRCL will have to submit the Independent Safety Assessor (ISA) signalling report to the CMRS. The safety commissioner will then examine the required documents and decide on a date for inspection of the corridor.

Following the inspection, the CMRS clearance is expected to take another one to two weeks, sources said. The corridor would then have to be formally inaugurated before passenger services can commence.

However, a senior BMRCL official said the corporation had not committed to September opening without the necessary approvals. “We said that the elevated section of Pink Line is expected to be inaugurated in September, subject to the completion of all statutory approvals and clearances,” the official said.

Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda inspected the corridor on September 2 and said civil and elevated works were ready. He had earlier indicated that the elevated section could be inaugurated and opened to commuters once the Centre provided the necessary approvals.

“We are ready. As soon as the date is given by the Government of India, this stretch will be inaugurated and opened to people for commuting,” Mr. Gowda had said.

The expected opening date has changed several times. After taking charge of the portfolio, the Minister had initially announced that the elevated section between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere would become operational by August 15, 2026. He had also said that the remaining underground section between Tavarekere and Nagawara was expected to be completed by March 2027.

The Pink Line is a 21.3-km corridor connecting Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru with Nagawara in the north. Of the total length, around 13.8 km is underground, while 7.5 km is elevated.

The underground section will pass through several important areas, including Dairy Circle, M.G. Road, Shivajinagar, and Tannery Road, providing a crucial north-south connection through the central parts of the city. The project has faced repeated delays and missed several earlier deadlines, leading to criticism from commuters who have been waiting for the corridor to become operational.

World.title: Mumbai Police seek clarification from Manoj Jarange over 'contradictory' statements on proposed protest
World.content:
The Mumbai Police have issued a notice to fasting Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange, seeking clarification on "contradictions" in his statements about his proposed protest in the State capital, officials said on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).

The move comes after the police repeatedly denied Mr. Jarange permission to stage a demonstration at Azad Maidan in South Mumbai.

Officials said Mr. Jarange had initially submitted a letter stating that he would protest alone, accompanied by only 50 people. However, officials said a large crowd of supporters was seen accompanying him as he set off for Mumbai from Jalna district on Tuesday (September 16, 2026).

Also Read | Maratha quota stir: Jarange Patil leaves for Mumbai as police deny nod for protest

In the notice dated September 15, the police asked Mr. Jarange to provide detailed information about the planned demonstration, including the list of volunteers, the total number of people attending, and details of the vehicles being used.

Police said Mr. Jarange's formal undertaking and his public statements are contradictory.

While informing authorities he would protest alone, the activist reportedly appealed to the Maratha community through the media to keep their bags packed and be ready to move to Mumbai upon his call to defend the quota.

Mr. Jarange on Wednesday (September 16) evening said he would stay at Potoda in Beed district for medical treatment and resume his journey to Mumbai to stage an agitation on Thursday (September 17) afternoon.

If anyone stopped him on the way, members of the Maratha community should set out for Maharashtra's capital, he said.

Mr. Jarange, whose hunger strike for reservation demands has entered the 19th day, reached Patoda in the early hours of Wednesday (September 16) and halted in the town as doctors advised him of immediate treatment due to severe dehydration and other health complications.

World.title: Bengaluru man’s song on crumbling infrastructure, potholes, flooding, traffic
World.content:
After exhausting all options, a Bengaluru commuter has now turned to artificial intelligence (AI) to generate a song titled Tax Me to request the government to build decent road infrastructure in the city.

The song about Bengaluru’s road infrastructure takes a tongue-in-cheek swipe at the city’s traffic, potholes, flooding, construction, and the endless digging of its roads. The song demands a basic for a city that the Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar says is being viewed internationally: a road that can simply be driven on.

Daily experience to song

Punit Vara, a 34-year-old techie residing near Choodasandra, who uploaded the song on YouTube, said that the song, including its lyrics, was completely AI-generated. It features Doddamara Road, which falls under the Anekal Assembly constituency, represented by A. Shivanna.

“For the past nine months, I drove my pregnant wife on Doddamara Road, which is in a pathetic condition, for regular doctor visits. I had to be extra careful, and it was highly dangerous, which prompted me to come up with this song,” he said. “Besides, I also drive on this road everday,” he added. Mr. Vara said he used his daily experiences of travelling on the road as prompts for generative AI, which came up with the lyrics. He later used another AI model to generate the song using the lyrics, he said.

Mr. Vara terms the song a satire anthem dedicated to every techie, parent, auto driver and commuter surviving Bengaluru’s “moonscape streets” every single day.

Potholes, traffic, construction

For many Bengalureans, the morning commute begins with a familiar ritual, which starts with checking the map, looking at the estimated travel time, and then adding a generous margin for the traffic that the maps could not possibly have accounted for. Now, that daily frustration has found a soundtrack.

“Pothole number 27,” a lyric in the song, takes a dig at the pathetic condition of Doddamara Road in the southeastern outskirts of Bengaluru, which is not very different from the other city roads.

“I pay my income tax. I pay my GST,” the song says, before listing the many other charges that accompany everyday life. The complaint, the song says, is not about wanting “gold-plated roads” or a perfect city. It is about basic infrastructure, including roads without potholes, sidewalks that can be walked on, buses that actually arrive, and streets that do not disappear under water during the monsoon.

Capturing the experience of navigating city’s roads with multiple projects on, the song says: “Metro above me. Digging below, flyover beside me. Nobody knows where to go.” The line captures the geography of a city, where construction seems endless.

World.title: Anto Augustine arrested by Excise in Abkari case
World.content:
Excise officials from Wayanad took into custody Anto Augustine, 38, managing director of Malayalam news channel Reporter TV, on Thursday (September 17, 2026) morning on charges of alleged possession of liquor in excess of the legally permissible limit.

He was taken into custody around 5 a.m. from the channel’s office at Kalamassery in Ernakulam. The move followed the reported recovery of 67 litres of liquor — beyond the permissible limit for possession — from his ancestral residence in Muttil South Village, Vythiri Taluk, Wayanad, on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) during a search operation conducted by the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing alleged financial fraud linked to the failed bid to bring the Argentine national team and Lionel Messi to Kochi for an international friendly last year.

Sharfudhin T., Excise Circle Inspector, Excise Circle Office, Kalpetta, filed an occurrence report in connection with the case registered under the Abkari Act before the Judicial First Class Magistrate’s Court, Sulthan Bathery, Wayanad, early on Thursday. The accused has been booked under Sections 55(a), 55(i), and 58 of the Kerala Abkari Act.

An Excise team led by Assistant Commissioner arrived at the Reporter TV office to take Mr. Augustine into custody. After the medical examination, Augustine will be taken to Wayanad and produced before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Sulthan Bathery in Wayanad, said excise sources.

Reportedly, Mr. Augustine initially insisted demanding that he be shown the occurrence report. Though the Excise team showed him a digital copy, he insisted on a hard copy, following which Perumbavoor Excise Circle Inspector Manoj Kumar came to the office with a copy.

The SIT had conducted day-long search operations at five locations in Ernakulam and Wayanad districts on Wednesday.

First accused

According to SIT sources, digital gadgets, documents, foreign currencies, and 67 litres of liquor were seized during the searches. The operations were carried out based on a First Information Report (FIR) registered by the Kalamassery police after a preliminary inquiry found prima facie grounds for a cognisable offence. Mr. Augustine was the first accused in the case as authorised signatory of the Reporter Broadcasting Private Limited. The company was named the second accused.

According to the FIR, the accused entered into a criminal conspiracy dating back to before December 20, 2024, when “illegal and fake” details were inserted into the agreement signed with the Argentina Football Association, with the intent of cheating the State government and the public for profiteering. The FIR further alleged that the accused conspired to gain custody of the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium at Kaloor by securing exemption from the ₹5 crore security deposit on September 26, 2025.

World.title: Manoj Jarange calls off 20-day-old fast, gives three months’ ‘ultimatum’ to government
World.content:
Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange on Thursday (September 17, 2026) called off his 20-day-old fast and warned the Maharashtra Government that he would take the protest to Mumbai if his demands over Maratha reservation were not considered in three months.

Mr. Jarange announced talks with a government delegation which included Ministers Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil, Dada Bhuse, MLC Prasad Lad and MLA Suresh Dhas and senior officials, at Patoda in Beed district.

Also Read | Maratha quota stir: Jarange Patil leaves for Mumbai as police deny nod for protest

The development came days after Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said the government won’t tolerate any intimidating tactics and questioned the timing of the agitation during the ongoing Ganesh festival.

During their meeting with Mr. Jarange in Patoda, where the activist had halted on the way to Mumbai, the delegation members informed him about the steps initiated by the state government for the Maratha quota.

Vikhe Patil suggested that Jarange should depute three representatives to monitor the progress of official work for considering his demands.

“It will take around three-four months to act on the Kolhapur and Satara gazette after a written comment is received from the advocate general,” the minister said, and urged Jarange to call off his hunger strike.

Mr. Jarange said he is firm on his demand for “official recognition” of historical administrative records like the Hyderabad Gazette, Satara Gazette, and Aundh Gazette so Marathas can prove Kunbi lineage and claim OBC reservation benefits.

“The government should give in writing that not a single ‘Kunbi’ record will be ignored. The chief minister should sign that paper,” he said.

Mr. Jarange said he will take his protest to Mumbai if the government reneges on the assurance given to him.

“If we are betrayed in the next three months, then we all will directly go to Mumbai along with our kids and women,” he said, and asked the over one lakh Marathas who had already gone to Mumbai to return to their homes.

Mr. Jarange, who set out from his Antarwali Sarati village in Jalna district, was scheduled to reach Mumbai on September 19 after passing through Ahilyanagar, Pune and Khopoli in Raigad district.

Last year, Mr. Jarange’s hunger strike at Azad Maidan brought South Mumbai to a standstill as thousands of his supporters poured into the city.

That agitation was called off on September 2, 2025, after the government accepted six of his eight demands and initiated steps for Kunbi classification certificates.

World.title: Yuvan Shankar Raja interview: On his first symphonic concert featuring his background scores
World.content:
“Drugs are legal here,” says a comment on a jukebox featuring his superhit tracks.

For a generation of Tamil film audiences who grew up in the 2000s, heartbreak and happiness came accompanied by a song tuned by Yuvan Shankar Raja. For them, his voice oozes intoxication – it’s no wonder that there are multiple playlists that are titled ‘U1 Drugs’.

But his voice alone will not be in the forefront of ‘Walking through the Rainbow’, a concert by the man this weekend in Chennai. A symphonic experience, it seeks to present a full-length orchestral experience of his iconic background scores that have been celebrated by Tamil cinema fans across the globe. Excerpts from an interview with the musician:

When did you conceptualise the idea of a symphonic presentation of your work, and why is this special?

I like to break regular formats. I went to Hans Zimmer’s concert in Abu Dhabi, and wished to do something on those lines. That took us to ‘Walking Through the Rainbow’, which is the first-ever concert built entirely around scores. We rehearsed the tracks with a symphony orchestra at Bangkok – some of them were very easy for them, but when it came to the music of 7G Rainbow Colony, they had to practise for almost half a day... which gave me the satisfaction that I had written a good score for that particular film. For me, be it the score or the songs, when I listen to my past work, I go back to the journey associated with it, and hence it is special. I believe audiences will experience the same feeling.

Your background music has become popular in its own right. When you score this, what are you trying to achieve that is different from what you do with a song?

Everything that we do is to elevate the film’s sequences. Take the ‘Bat Theme’ in Chennai 600028, for instance. Venkat (director Venkat Prabhu) already had a tune from my father’s work [Ilaiyaraaja’s ‘Apoorva Sagodargal’ emotional theme] for that situation, but I created a trap version around it. Before I embarked on Paruthiveeran’s background score, I heard as much as possible of my father’s and AR Rahman’s folk work and decided to go the opposite way. I kept it as raw as possible. If you hear the score even today, the nadaswaram player had made some mistakes. But I left it as such – because I wanted it to be like a thiruvizha, where such missteps occur.

A song has lyrics and singers to steer audience emotion. With background music, there are no words. How do you find that emotional language?

My scores and themes are usually not based on the songs in the film. I prefer taking the hard way, and do a score that has a connection with the songs of the film. Sometimes, the visual inspires me – Mankatha’s chase sequence is one example. Sometimes, we take English scores and paste them on for a sequence – not as a rip off, but to understand the sound spectrum. Simbu’s Manmadhan was done like that.

You’re known for both romance and mass music. Which is tougher to crack?

Truth be told, both are not tough. Your mind has to be like a clean slate when you start works. Creativity is about flow. If there’s something amiss in the office, I cannot work. If my mind is clutter free, music flows. My mind goes back to ‘Naane Varuven’, a score that Selvaraghavan and I worked for almost seven days. Dhanush heard it, and scrapped everything. But I managed to complete the entire score within 24 hours, because my mind was free. As a composer, I am like clay. I can mould myself according to what the makers seek in a project. This is a quality that I picked from my father.

Your father recently presented ‘Valiant’, a classical symphony. How inspiring was that achievement for you as a musician to devise your own symphonic presentation?

I started composing music when I was 16, much before I had the life experiences to score for the subjects I was taking on. My father and his music were the biggest foundation for my inclination towards background score. Even when I have a tough sequence in front of me, I take it as a challenge.

What happens when you’re composing music and hit a roadblock?

Nothing. I just have some dessert (laughs).

Did you grow up listening to your father’s work and wanting to become like him?

When I was in school, my only exposure to my dad’s songs was through Oliyum Oliyum on TV. They would play the programme loudly at home and I would happen to listen to the songs in the background even as I was playing. As time went by, I kept listening to hip-hop and RnB. I was in a zone where I thought, ‘We need to bring this kind of music here.’ I decided to do a private album, for which I listened to RD Burman and MS Viswanathan’s work extensively. When I came to appa’s work, the vehicle stopped (laughs).

After becoming an established composer yourself, how much did your relationship with your father’s music change?

I had gone to Melbourne to mix Sarvam (2009), and on the flight, I happened to hear ‘Netru Indrum Neram’ and another song in Tik Tik Tik (1981)on loop. I was taken aback by how he had managed to pull off those sounds, back in the Eighties. The minute I came back, I rushed to him to understand how that was done. Then, I started noticing more of his background scores and realised that he is an encyclopaedia when it comes to music.

Today social media is filled with a debate pitting Ilaiyaraaja versus AR Rahman. As a music fan, how do you view this debate?

I don’t see it as a debate. I know ARR very well; his son, AR Ameen, hangs out with me all the time. There are no walls between composers. We all speak to each other. I’m unable to understand this from a fan’s point of view.

Actor Ajith’s Dheena (2001) was a turning point in your career. You share a warm camaraderie with him; last year, we saw you bonding with him in Dubai when he was practising for the Le Mans race. As a film industry colleague, how inspiring is it to see him pursue motor racing?

It is vera level to watch him. It’s very easy for us to speak about car racing from a distance, but I have witnessed his struggles up close. He showed me recorded footage from his previous races. It is extremely inspiring to watch his passion and intensity.

People close to you tell me that you are deeply spiritual. You converted to Islam. Has your spiritual pursuit influenced your musical journey too?

It has helped handle the stress around me. Be it losing someone or winning a big award, spirituality has helped me handle both these ends of the spectrum of life. It has helped me be more at peace.

Yuvan’s ‘Walking Through the Rainbow’ will be held at Nehru Indoor Stadium on September 19. Tickets on District

World.title: Islamabad, Beijing activate joint border commission
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and China on Wednesday operationalised a long pending joint mechanism for managing their common border, with Islamabad des­cribing the move as a significant milestone in bilateral relations and a step toward closer coordination on border management, trade and cross-border connectivity.

“The inaugural meeting of the Commission was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Islamabad,” the Foreign Office said in a statement.

The meeting was co-led by Li Ya, deputy director general of the Department of Boundary and Ocean Affairs at China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Bilal Mahmood Chaudhary, director general for China at Pakistan’s Foreign Office.

The FO described the ope­r­ationalisation of the Pakis­tan-China Boundary Joint Com­m­ission as a “significant milestone for Pak­istan-China relations”, saying it would set “the stage for enh­anced cooperation in border management, joint border surveys, trade flows and people to people connectivity.”

The commission has its origins in the 2013 Agre­ement on the Boundary Mana­gement System signed during the visit of then Chinese Premier Li Keqiang to Islamabad. Article 45 of the agreement provides for establishment of the joint commission to oversee implementation of the border management arrangements.

The mechanism would provide an institutional framework for dealing with practical issues along the border, including maintenance and inspection of the boundary, joint surveys, boundary marker issues, management of cross-border facilities and handling of incidents involving the border.

Its activation also gives the two countries a mechanism for regular coordination on a border that is important for movement between Pakistan and China, including thr­ough the Khunjerab crossing, and for trade and connectivity linked to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

The new commission is distinct from the Joint Boundary Demarcation Commission that was established under the Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement of March 2, 1963. The earlier commission had a specific and essentially one time mandate to conduct surveys, establish boundary markers, prepare detailed maps and set out the alignment of the boundary.

Its work ended after the signing of the protocol and maps completing the demarcation process. The 1963 agreement was signed in Beijing by then-Pakistani foreign minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and his Chinese counterpart Chen Yi.

It also provided that, following a settlement of the Kashmir dispute between Pakistan and India, the relevant sovereign authority would reopen negotiations with China on the boundary.

The 2013 agreement, by contrast, established a continuing system for managing the already demarcated boundary, including provisions for dealing with boundary markers and cross-border infrastructure. The agreement says that if a marker cannot be restored at its original location, the joint commission can determine another suitable location, provided the boundary line itself is not altered.

India, which disputes the validity of the 1963 agreement and regards the territory covered by it as part of Occupied Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, rejected the new mechanism.

“We have seen reports in this regard. Our position on this matter is clear and consistent. There is no boundary between Pakistan and China. We reject the so-called Joint Commission, which is without any legal basis,” Ind­ian Foreign Ministry spokesman Randhir Jaiswal said.

For Pakistan and China, however, the commission provides a new institutional arrangement for managing their border relationship and dealing with practical issues that have emerged since the 2013 agreement, while leaving the broader territorial positions of the parties unchanged.

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs6.88 per litre, HSD by Rs5.62 per litre
World.content:
The government on Wednesday increased the price of petrol by Rs6.88 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5.62 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs391.22 per litre while HSD will cost Rs421.45 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 17 (Thursday).

According to Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the increase is primarily linked to higher petrol and diesel prices in the international market.

The regulator said the prices were revised based on international market rates, premiums and other relevant factors.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Pakistan to stand by Saudi Arabia 'practically and diplomatically' if Yemen conflict escalates: Asif
World.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Wednesday said Pakistan would “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalated.

Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen’s Houthis accused the rebels of targeting the holy city of Makkah, sparking outrage across the Muslim world and deepening the conflict roiling the region.

However, the Houthis swiftly rejected Riyadh’s report as a “lie” that it shot down a drone from the rebels heading towards Makkah.

“If the situation escalates, we will stand with Saudi Arabia, both practically and diplomatically,” he said while speaking on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shehzaib Khanzada Ke Saath’.

Commenting on the Pakistan-Turkiye-Saudi Arabia trilateral agreement — the Makkah Defence Alliance — he affirmed that an agreement was in place.

However, he said that even if there had been no such agreement, Pakistan was bound by an “eternal agreement to respond if the holy sites come under attack”.

“There are some worldly agreements, too, and they have their own sanctity and obligations, but protecting the holy sites is our religious duty,” he said.

Asif maintained that Muslims around the world did not need an agreement to act if the holy sites in Makkah or Madina came under attack. “There is no need to activate any agreement,” he said.

The defence minister maintained that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

“There is absolutely no ambiguity,” he asserted.

Asked about any military or political engagement with the Houthis, Asif said he could not disclose details, adding that strategies at this level were not meant to be made public.

However, he reiterated that Pakistan was bound by the agreement.

“Under the trilateral agreement, if the territorial integrity of a country comes under threat, the agreement will be activated and the other two countries will proceed to protect it in fulfilment of their obligations,” he said. “The situation has arrived.”

On the US-Israeli war on Iran, Asif said it had become clear, a month into the conflict, that Israel’s calculations had not produced the expected results.

“Israel sucked America into this war as a combatant party, but under the present circumstances, the world and the region need to realise that Israel is the real culprit,” he said.

“Until Israel is confronted by a joint alliance, it will remain a threat to the region. The Zionist lobby also forces the US to join Israel’s wars.”

Sharing his personal view on possible Iranian support for the Houthis, he said Iran, as a state, might not be backing the group as it was already embroiled in another conflict in the Middle East.

“This would be a diplomatic error if Iran were to take the side of the Houthis, but the chances are minimal. Escalating the conflict into another theatre is not a wise decision and could turn it into a wider conflict,” Asif said.

Fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government has dragged in Riyadh, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea.

Last week’s lightning offensive saw the group seize control of the entirety of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital artery for Saudi oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes off the Strait of Hormuz strategic shipping route.

Pakistan’s stance

Earlier today, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that the defence alliance has no “regional aspirations”, adding that it is intended for collective deterrence.

The military spokesperson made the remarks during an interview on Al Arabiya English’s programme ‘Global News Today’, during a conversation with the host, Tom Burges Watson.

“It formalises Pakistan’s decades-old relationship with the kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the brotherly country of Turkiye in the domains of collective deterrence and defence,” he said.

Watson asked whether the pact was primarily a defensive cooperation or the beginning of a broader strategic alliance. To that, Lt Gen Chaudhry asserted that the pact was defensive, as its name implied.

“It is defensive. There’s nothing aggressive. There are no regional aspirations. It is collective deterrence,” he said, adding that the agreement was also “complementary”.

During the interview, Lt Gen Chaudhry was also asked whether he saw the defence agreement becoming a part of the wider, Muslim-world security architecture.

He replied that there was nothing in the pact that stated that it was a Muslim alliance, adding that it was an alliance for regional stability.

“It is not a club that is being made for only Muslim countries,” he said, adding that decisions on its expansion were to be taken by the leadership of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

“This agreement, this alliance can always encompass new, willing partners who also believe in regional peace, stability and security, [and] who have a shared vision of non-aggression, non-interference and collective deterrence.

“But that’s for the leadership of these three countries to decide; the how and when part,” he elaborated.

The joint defence pact was signed on Aug 7 and provides that an attack on one member state would be treated as an attack on all. Its inaugural meeting was held in Istanbul on Aug 31, where it was decided that Pakistan would initially head the alliance’s secretariat for three years.

Since its signing, there has been conversation about the possibility of its expansion, with Turkiye initially suggesting the possibility of Egypt’s inclusion. Though there has been no confirmation from Cairo.

From Pakistan, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar clarified soon after the signing that the pact was defensive in nature, with the latter saying that it was also “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles.

However, when Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjah Haider Khan was asked about possibility of the pact’s expansion during a weekly media briefing last week, he said an expansion was not on the cards at that point.

The three countries first needed to solidify the new organisation before considering opening it to other states with similar threat perceptions and requirements, he explained.

World.title: Google-Pakistan deal raises data privacy concerns
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Media watchdog Freedom Network has penned an open letter to Google and the government, seeking to know what sa­­feguards will ensure that the tech giant’s recent partnership with Pakistan strengthens the country’s digital economy without creating a backdoor for surveillance, censorship or unrestricted access to citizens’ personal information.

The Islamabad-based watchdog welcomed the signing of memoranda of understanding and agreements be­­tween Google and the governm­e­­nt after the company opened its of­­fice in Pakistan to advance the country’s digital vision, but expres­sed ap­­prehensions that the tech company and the government had not made details of their agreements public.

“A big question is what exactly has been agreed? Will the government or Google publish all MoUs, agreements, contracts or other arra­ngements signed between them? If some provisions must remain confidential, who decided that and under what law?” Freedom Network asked in its alert shared with the media through a press release.

The media watchdog asked if there were any undisclosed commitments concerning access to user data, content, metadata or government databases. “Under what circumstances can Pakistani authorities request information about Google users? Will every request require a valid legal process and judicial oversight? Will Google reject requests that are overly broad, vague or inconsistent with fundamental rights?”

Media watchdog seeks details of MoUs, agreements

Freedom Network was explicit in asking if any protection or unambiguous safeguards against government access to journalists’ Gmail, Google Drive, photos, YouTube accounts, search-related information or other data that could reveal confidential sources were part of the agreements and MoUs.

The watchdog asked Google to commit itself to not removing any content merely because a government agency asks, or that requests for blocking or removal shall be assessed under transparent legal standards and users shall receive notice and an opportunity to challenge decisions where legally possible.

Freedom Network also worried about where Pakistani citizens’ data would be stored as the country is developing a national data-governance framework that urges data sovereignty, minimum disclosure and citizens’ right to know who has accessed their information. “Will Pakistani users’ data be stored in Pakistan, overseas, or both?” it asked Google.

“There should not be informal or undocumented data-sharing arrangements between Google and the Pakistan government.”

The press release quoted the media watchdog as asking the tech company: “Who independently will audit Google’s compliance with privacy and human-rights safeguards in Pakistan? The answer should not be simply the government.”

World.title: US Fed delivers first rate hike since 2023
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday raised interest rates in the world’s largest economy by 25 basis points to tackle stubbornly high inflation, a move sure to anger President Donald Trump, who has demanded lower rates.

The Fed’s Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously to raise rates to between 3.75 and 4.00 per cent, citing “elevated” inflation and adding that the rate hike would support a “timelier return” to its 2pc target for the metric.

Addressing a press conference after the rate decision, US Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh stre­ssed that the central bank’s decision to raise interest rates, the first since 2023, was not influenced by financial markets.

“We made this decision today based on our assessment of the situation,” Warsh told the press conference. “I’ll observe market prices and see what they have to say. But today was our decision.”

He said that the central bank’s independence comes from staying focused on its objectives, in comments that come amid political pressure for lower interest rates.

“Part of the independence of the Federal Reserve is we stay in our lane,” Warsh said. “We let people that do trade policy and fiscal policy stay in their lane too. That’s how we can stand up here and call them the way we see them.

“Our predominant focus is on the price stability side of our mandate. The plain fact is that inflation is too high, and has been for too long,” he told a press conference.

A majority of Fed policymakers expect at least one more rate hike to be necessary before the end of the year, according to the central bank’s Summary of Economic Projections, also published Wednesday.

World.title: IAEA safeguards deal for Chashma-5 nuclear power plant secured
World.content:
• 1,200MW reactor’s dome placed early; commissioning set for 2028

• Talks held with China on N-cooperation

ISLAMABAD: The Inte­rnational Atomic Energy Agency and Pakistan on Wednesday signed a safeguards agreement for the 1,200-megawatt Chashma-5 nuclear power plant to bolster the country’s energy security while ensuring international non-proliferation standards.

IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi and Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission Chairman Raja Ali Raza Anwar signed the pact at the agency’s headquarters in Vienna. The signing took place on the sidelines of the 70th IAEA General Conference.

Shan Zhongde, chairman of the China Atomic Energy Authority, witnessed the ceremony. The agreement, which governs the application of safeguards at Unit-5 of the Chashma plant, was unanimously approved by the IAEA Board of Governors in March.

According to a statement on the signing, the agreement marks a critical step toward implementing safeguards for the new facility.

Officials noted that it reflects the international community’s continued confidence in Pakistan’s commitment to the peaceful use of nuclear energy and its adherence to global non-proliferation obligations.

Construction of the Chashma-5 (C-5) facility is progressing rapidly, with early completion of the reactor’s dome placement among its recent milestones.

Scheduled for commissioning in 2028, the unit is expected to add a substantial source of low-carbon, low-cost electricity to Pakistan’s national grid to support climate objectives and sustainable economic growth.

Pakistan currently operates six nuclear power plants with a combined installed capacity of 3,530 megawatts. According to the Atomic Energy Commission, these plants have maintained an average capacity factor exceeding 90pc.

Officials highlighted that the country possesses more than 100 reactor-years of operational experience, maintaining a strong record of safe, secure and safeguarded operations under international standards.

Prior to the signing ceremony, Pakistani and Chinese delegations met to discuss ongoing and future cooperation in the peaceful applications of nuclear science and technology.

Anwar led the Pakistani delegation, while Zhongde headed the Chinese group. Mohammad Kamran Akhtar Malik, Pakistan’s ambassador to Austria and permanent representative to the IAEA, also participated in the bilateral discussions.

World.title: African elephant Madhubala on ‘antibiotics’ after collapsing at Karachi’s Safari Park
World.content:
KARACHI: Despite carrying out several tests, including an X-ray, over the past two days, the authorities in Safari Park remain clueless about what caused the sudden collapse of African elephant Madhubala in her enclosure, it emerged on Wednesday.

Responding to queries, a spokesperson for the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) said that Madhubala suffered from “acute weakness and low immunity levels” following prolonged treatment for tuberculosis and that’s what caused her sudden fall.

“While all her laboratory tests are just fine, she is being given antibiotics as a precautionary measure on the advice of a senior local vet. No fracture has been detected in the X-ray,” KMC spokesperson Daniyal Alishan Siyal told Dawn, adding that all medical reports were emailed to Sri Lankan wildlife health specialist Dr Buddhika for final assessment.

When asked why she is being given antibiotics when no bacterial infection has been detected, he said, “I am told that she has elevated infection markers, though no specific cause has been detected.”

The African elephant is suffering from ‘acute weakness and low immunity levels’

Madhubala, he pointed out, could now stand on her feet and the supporting crate belt had been removed.

On the swelling on her right hind thigh, he claimed that, “It was caused by her fall.”

He rejected the information that Madhubala was acutely dehydrated on the day of her fall because there wasn’t sufficient water to keep her cool on hot days.

“There were no power breakdowns that could lead to water issues,” Mr Siyal said.

Foot abscess recovery?

Safari Park Director Amjad Zaidi two days ago stated that it’s apparently the swelling on her right thigh, which was preventing her from using her leg. He had also stated that Madhubala had “recovered” from a foot infection.

Sources stated Madhubala’s swelling on her right hind thigh might be indicating spread of abscess from the foot (on the same affected leg) that she had been fighting for some period.

“Elevated infection markers mean her body’s immune system is reacting to a problem, though her test results cannot tell the exact cause,” a senior vet shared.

Steady signs of improvement: KMC

The KMC released a press statement on Madhubala’s condition, stating that the elephant is showing steady signs of improvement and continues to receive round-the-clock veterinary care and close medical monitoring.

“The latest health assessments have revealed several encouraging signs of improvement. Madhubala is now able to stand independently without harness support, marking a positive development in her recovery. Her vital parameters remain stable, while she continues to maintain a good appetite and remains alert and responsive,” it says.

It further adds that Madhubala is undergoing daily health assessments and blood tests, while X-rays of her hind quarters are also being conducted regularly.

“These diagnostic procedures are being carried out with the support of the Sindh Institute of Animal Health, enabling veterinary experts to closely monitor her physical condition and evaluate her progress.

“Madhubala’s dedicated keeper team remains with her around the clock. The keepers, who have been closely involved in her daily care, are working in close coordination with the veterinary team to ensure that she receives appropriate nutrition, care, supervision and support throughout her recovery,” it adds.

Madhubala had been in solitary confinement at Karachi Zoo following the tragic death of her companion Noor Jehan who died in 2023 after a tragic fall in her enclosure.

Noor Jehan’s autopsy report released by the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) showed that she died from a severe blood parasitic infection and internal trauma combined with a lack of proper medical care.

Left alone at the zoo, Madhubala was successfully relocated to Safari Park where she was reunited with her sisters, Sonia and Malika, in November 2024, under the supervision of Four Paws — an international animal welfare organisation that worked extensively with the KMC for elephant care.

The success story of her reunion faded soon as Sonia died a month later after collapsing in her Safari enclosure.

Lab reports later showed that she suffered from multiple chronic illnesses, affecting almost all vital organs, indicating prolonged neglect in her care and failure in timely diagnosis.

Successive deaths of captive elephants raised public outcry, forcing the KMC to set up an 18-member body to look after Madhubala and Malika, both of whom were diagnosed with tuberculosis.

The four female elephants were brought to Karachi from Tanzania in 2010 at a very young age under a controversial arrangement.

Published in Dawn, September 17th, 2026

World.title: Dealers await answers as fuel subsidy rollout begins
World.content:
• Petroleum dealers lament lack of clarity on payment mechanism, timeline

• PM wants facilitation desks to help people trying to buy subsidised fuel

• Ogra attributes hike to elevated crude prices despite decline in int’l rates

ISLAMABAD: Even as members of the public who have signed up for the PM’s Fuel Relief Scheme queued up at fuel pumps late on Wednesday night, petroleum dealers were still not clear about the mechanism whereby they would be compensated.

The concern was voiced by the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) during a presser in Karachi, where its chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh said that no fuel pump could afford to bear a loss of Rs100 per litre without clarity on how they will be compensated.

He claimed that between the petroleum ministry, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) and even the finance ministry, no one had been able to answer their questions.

“Officials from Ogra and oil marketing companies say that the petroleum ministry will possibly pay the subsidy amount, whereas ministry officials maintain that payments will be made by the finance ministry, while finance ministry officials assure us that the State Bank will release the funds in a day or two,“ Mr Bakhsh added.

A day earlier, the National Steering Com­mittee on Fuel Subsidy — chaired by Deputy PM Ishaq Dar — had ordered that payments to fuel stations under the PM’s scheme be processed within 24 hours through the State Bank of Pakistan.

However, Mr Bakhsh said the federal government had assured dealers that they would be taken into confidence before the launch of the fuel relief package, but lamented that no such consultation took place.

”The government has to understand that if payments are not reimbursed in time, many dealers will stop participating in [the scheme], as many previous promises were also not fulfilled by the government,” he added.

PPDA Vice Chairman Tariq Hassan said that around 14,000 dealers across the country have been trying desperately to contact the government over the past three days, adding that whenever Islamabad wants to enforce something, it stops communication.

Another vice chairman, Anwar Kamal, said that if the scheme was to be successful, the government must negotiate with dealers, adding that dealers could not afford to have billions tied up for a long period under this scheme.

Mr Bakhsh later told Dawn they had been invited to a virtual meeting with the relevant federal secretary on Thursday morning.

He added that Ogra officials had also reached out to brief him, but he had asked for that information in writing, so he could relay that to the members of his association.

Facilitation desks

Earlier, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered authorities to set up facilitation desks comprising administration officials, volunteers and petrol pump staff to assist citizens in easily obtaining fuel subsidy under the special relief scheme, which was rolled out across the country at Wednesday midnight, following the launch of the pilot phase in Islamabad.

Presiding over a meeting to review progress on the scheme, PM Shehbaz directed that personnel deployed at the facilitation desks should guide eligible citizens and provide them with all possible assistance in registration and other necessary procedures.

The prime minister also asked the relevant authorities to remain proactive in creating public awareness about the scheme, which will benefit people from all four provinces, Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.

The meeting was informed that the scheme had been designed in a simple and easy-to-understand manner for the public. Only four pieces of information were required for registration: the applicant’s CNIC number, vehicle number plate, province of registration and vehicle registration date.

Complete details of the fuel subsidy scheme are available in Urdu on www.pmfuelrelief.pk.

According to an official, the number of successful registrations was gradually rising, while provincial governments were extending “full cooperation” for nationwide implementation of the scheme.

Oil prices

Meanwhile, notifying fresh POL rates on Wednesday night, Ogra attributed the steep hikes to elevated international crude oil and petroleum product prices.

The price of high-speed diesel was increased by Rs5.62 per litre to Rs421.45, while petrol became costlier by Rs6.88 per litre, taking its new price to Rs391.22 per litre.

However, Reuters reported on Wednesday night that oil prices fell in the open market on reports that Saudi Arabia was offering additional crude cargoes through Oman eased some concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.

Brent crude futures fell $2.92, or 2.7 per cent, to settle at $105.83 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate futures fell $3.40, or 3.2pc, to close at $102.43, Reuters reported.

Saudi Arabia is offering more loadings of crude oil to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfers off Oman’s Sohar port, people familiar with the matter said, blunting some of the hit to global supply from attacks on the country’s East-West pipeline to the Red Sea.

Oil prices had gained more than $3 in the previous session after shipping industry sources said crude loadings at Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea export hub of Yanbu had been suspended and Riyadh had cancelled some cargo deliveries to European customers.

The suspension followed strikes on the East-West pipeline, which feeds the Saudi port of Yanbu. It became the main Saudi outlet for oil exports after Iran began blockading the Strait of Hormuz after US and Israeli attacks on the country.
